section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How is drinking alcohol and driving classified?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem,b:A serious traffic safety problem,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks
note: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is a serious safety issue and greatly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to:
options: a:Other drivers already in the intersection,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:Pedestrians only if they are in a crosswalk
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians and bicyclists in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on:
options: a:Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic,b:Whether there is a stop sign present,c:Whether you used your turn signal
note: The gap needed to cross or turn depends on road surface, weather, and the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factors affect your vehicle's braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition.,b:Only the age of the vehicle.,c:Only the number of passengers.,d:Only the color of the vehicle.
note: Braking distance depends on how fast you are traveling, the state of your brakes and tires, and road surface conditions such as wetness or ice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you hit an unattended parked car and can't find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written note with your name, address, and accident details,b:Stay until the police arrive,c:Assume you have done enough and leave
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle, leave a written notice with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident if the owner cannot be located.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by which color lines?
options: a:White lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Red lines.,d:Green lines.
note: White lines (solid or broken) are used to separate lanes moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must the driver produce?
options: a:Their driver license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.,b:Only proof of insurance.,c:Only proof of registration.,d:Only their license.
note: Drivers must present their license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance when requested by law enforcement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes,b:Only during daylight hours,c:At any time regardless of conditions
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you reach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,d:Drive through if the intersection seems clear.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding the right-of-way, just like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross,b:Always stop at the curb before crossing,c:Possibly run into the street without looking
note: Children can act unpredictably; reduce speed and be prepared to stop at any time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane indicate the boundaries of:
options: a:A bicycle lane,b:A pedestrian crosswalk,c:A no-passing zone for vehicles only
note: Two solid white lines can mark a crosswalk; drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Taking drugs along with alcohol generally:
options: a:Increases the risk of causing a crash,b:Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone,c:Lessens the effect of alcohol on driving ability
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) increases impairment and crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,c:Back up on the exit ramp.,d:Signal and cross multiple lanes at once to get back.
note: Do not stop or back up on the highway; proceed to the next exit and safely turn around to return to the desired exit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles,b:They must use the bicycle lane,c:They are limited to half a lane
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane just like other vehicles and should be treated accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Immediately stomp on the brakes,b:Do not immediately use your brakes; take your foot off the gas,c:Keep accelerating to reach the shoulder quickly
note: Take your foot off the gas, avoid sudden braking, gradually slow, then steer to a safe place to stop.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating; do not remain beside them for extended periods.,b:Always pass on the right, even in tight spaces.,c:Flash your lights to get their attention.,d:Drive directly behind them very close.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots at the sides and rear; avoid lingering alongside and give them plenty of space when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a railroad crossing that has no active signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if you see or hear a train,c:Assume all crossings have signals and proceed normally
note: At unprotected crossings slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if one is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A double solid yellow centerline down a two-lane road means:
options: a:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous — always look and listen for trains.,b:Safe to cross without looking.,c:A place safe to park.
note: Railroad crossings are hazardous; always look both ways, listen, and obey signals or flaggers before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The end of the reduced speed school zone.,b:The beginning of a reduced speed zone.,c:The area with more children present.
note: The 'End school zone' sign marks the point where the special school zone speed limit and restrictions end.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why must drivers be more cautious at night?
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night,b:There is a larger volume of traffic at night,c:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards; headlights must be used from half hour after sunset to half hour before sunrise.

question: When your visibility decreases, your first response should be to:
options: a:Turn on your headlights,b:Reduce your speed,c:Turn on your windshield wipers
note: Reducing speed gives you more time to react when visibility is limited or road conditions are hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is separated by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines,b:White lines,c:Red lines
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate traffic moving the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash mean?
options: a:The action shown is forbidden,b:Drivers should come to a complete stop,c:Some drivers must yield
note: A red circle with a slash over a symbol indicates that the depicted action is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reduce visibility by reflecting off moisture.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which recommendation does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle,b:Keep the windshield clean,c:Be aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility
note: Carrying a flashlight is not one of the primary measures for safe night driving; the focus should be on clean windshield and avoiding dark-tint that reduces visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection simultaneously with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right,b:The vehicle approaching from the left,c:The vehicle whose driver honks first
note: At intersections of similar roads without controls, yield to traffic coming from your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass another vehicle when:
options: a:On a hill or curve,b:You are driving at the speed limit,c:You are approaching an intersection with wide visibility
note: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, or when sight distance is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do?
options: a:Moved the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Not move the injured unnecessarily. Keep the injured warm and administer first aid.
note: Avoid moving injured persons unless necessary; keep them warm, control severe bleeding, and wait for professional medical help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do regulatory signs tell drivers?
options: a:What drivers must or must not do,b:That the area is especially dangerous,c:They are warning signs (diamond-shaped, yellow/green)
note: Regulatory signs instruct drivers about legal requirements (speed limits, turn restrictions, etc.) and are often rectangular with black on white markings.

question: When should you reduce speed due to road or environmental conditions?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, at intersections or railroad crossings, and when roads are wet or slippery,b:Only when you see a police car,c:Only when entering a highway with traffic
note: Slow down in areas or conditions that reduce safety: narrow/winding roads, intersections, crossings, and slippery surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the posted speed limit sign represent?
options: a:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:A recommended speed for heavy traffic only.,c:The exact safe speed for all drivers.
note: The posted limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust downward for adverse conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield if a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The driver must yield to the pedestrian,b:The pedestrian must yield to the driver,c:Whoever started moving last must yield
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in intersections without traffic signals to prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, you should:
options: a:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent the emergency vehicle from passing,b:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel (pull to side when safe)
note: You must allow emergency vehicles using sirens or lights a clear path; pull over to the side and stop if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out due to power failure at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Park and wait for power to return,b:Turn on your hazards and proceed without stopping,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield in turn
note: If traffic signals are dark due to a power failure and there is no officer directing traffic, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in the order of arrival; if you arrive at the same time as another vehicle, yield to the driver on your right and proceed with caution.

question: When may a driver with a probationary license use a telecommunications device while driving?
options: a:Only to call 911 in an emergency,b:When they are a high school graduate,c:Texting but not talking on the phone
note: In Indiana, drivers with a probationary license (under 21) are generally prohibited from using any telecommunications device while driving, including hands-free, except to call 911 in an emergency. This rule is meant to reduce distraction for new drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should end up in:
options: a:The left lane of the one-way street (closest to the lane you came from),b:The center of the one-way street,c:The right lane of the one-way street
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from. This usually means turning from the left lane of the two-way street into the left lane of the one-way street, which keeps traffic organized and reduces conflict with other vehicles.

question: What does a red arrow signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and then proceed when clear without waiting for a green signal.,b:Slow and proceed through the intersection.,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.
note: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and stay stopped. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until the signal changes to a green arrow or a circular green light that permits the movement.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is the driver's responsibility?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is looking at their phone.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and take all reasonable actions to avoid striking them.,c:Only yield when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,d:Proceed unless the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must always use due care to avoid hitting pedestrians. You must yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians and take all reasonable actions to avoid striking them, even if they are crossing where or when they should not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street,b:Close to the left side of the street,c:As close to the right side of the road as possible
note: Before making a right turn, you should position your vehicle as close to the right curb or edge of the roadway as is safe and practical. This helps prevent cutting across lanes and keeps traffic flowing smoothly.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A solid yellow light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A steady green light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, being prepared to stop if needed. It does not require a full stop unless other traffic or conditions make it necessary.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when parking.,b:Only when backing up.,c:Before changing lanes
note: Before changing lanes, you must quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles that are alongside you but just behind your field of view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use the entrance ramp to merge onto a crowded freeway?
options: a:Always stop before merging.,b:Yield to emergency vehicles on the ramp.,c:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap. Stopping on the ramp is dangerous unless traffic or a control device requires it.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving generally have what level of control?
options: a:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,c:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
note: Any amount of alcohol can impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time, so drivers who have been drinking do not have full control over their bodies, minds, or vehicles. This reduced control makes driving after drinking unsafe at any level.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:
options: a:Refuse to let other cars pass you,b:Pull off the road and let traffic pass when safe,c:Decrease your speed further
note: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is building up behind you, you are impeding the normal flow of traffic. When it is safe, pull off the road or into a turnout area and let other vehicles pass so traffic can move smoothly.

question: What does an orange traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A railroad crossing ahead.,b:A school zone.,c:Road work or maintenance ahead.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control, such as construction, road work, or maintenance zones. They warn drivers to be prepared for workers, equipment, lane shifts, or reduced speeds ahead.

question: When you are near heavy trucks, others should allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop. When driving near trucks, allow extra space in front of them, avoid cutting in too closely, and do not assume they can stop as quickly as a smaller vehicle.

question: What is the most important speed-management rule for curves?
options: a:Maintain or increase speed as you enter the curve.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Brake hard while in the curve.
note: Slow down before entering a curve so you can steer smoothly and keep traction. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding, especially on wet or loose surfaces, because your tires are trying to both turn and slow at the same time.

question: What can happen if a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:They are immune from traffic stops.,b:They can be ticketed like other road users.,c:They will always receive only a warning.,d:They are always excused because they are bicyclists.
note: Bicyclists generally must follow the same traffic laws as drivers: stopping at red lights and stop signs, yielding when required, and signaling turns. If they disobey these laws, they can be stopped and ticketed just like drivers of motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic light means what?
options: a:Merging traffic,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians or other vehicles that are already in or entering the intersection.

question: What is the correct action when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?
options: a:Stop in the middle of the intersection and wait.,b:Try to reach your destination before it arrives.,c:Pull over to the right side of the road and stop.,d:Continue driving but attempt to remain out of its way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it passes. If you are in an intersection, first clear the intersection, then pull over and stop as soon as it is safe.

question: Before starting the ignition, what safety action should you take?
options: a:Only check that backseat passengers have buckled.,b:Make sure the radio is off.,c:Start the engine and then buckle up.,d:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are restrained.
note: Before turning the key or pressing the start button, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers, especially children, are properly restrained. Making this a habit ensures everyone is protected from the moment the vehicle starts moving.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Take the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Proceed normally.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right‑of‑way. Blind pedestrians may not be able to see you or judge your speed, so you must give them extra time and space to cross safely.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood it generally:
options: a:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly,b:Makes you less confident,c:Slows your reaction time
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your central nervous system. As your blood alcohol concentration rises, your reaction time gets slower, your judgment and coordination are impaired, and it becomes harder to respond quickly to hazards on the road.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Only exchange insurance information and leave,b:Continue driving to the nearest police station,c:Stop
note: If you are involved in a serious crash, you must stop at or near the scene. After stopping, check for injuries, call 911 if anyone is hurt, provide reasonable help if you can do so safely, and exchange information as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A single broken yellow centerline down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and you may pass when it is safe,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed,c:You are not permitted to pass
note: A single broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is broken, vehicles in either direction may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Never; keep the same distance at all times.,b:When following a large vehicle that blocks your vision,c:Only when following a motorcycle.,d:When traffic is light and visibility is good.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever you need more time to see and react, such as when following a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather, at higher speeds, or when following motorcycles or bicycles, which can stop or swerve more quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Increase your speed,c:Come to a complete stop
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, being prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles if necessary. It does not require a full stop unless needed for safety.

question: How long do points assessed for traffic violations remain on your Indiana driving record?
options: a:Six months,b:Two years,c:Nine months
note: In Indiana, points from traffic violations stay on your driving record for two years from the date of conviction. After two years they no longer count toward possible penalties based on point totals.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the proper immediate response?
options: a:Turn off the ignition while driving at highway speed.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure to the brake,c:Shift into park immediately while moving.,d:Reach down to manually lift the pedal while keeping speed.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep control of the vehicle by quickly shifting to neutral, then apply steady, firm braking and steer to a safe place off the road. Once stopped, turn off the engine. Do not turn the ignition off or shift into park while moving, as this can cause loss of steering or damage the transmission.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light in which situation?
options: a:Only if turning left.,b:If you are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow.,c:Only if you are speeding up to clear the intersection.,d:If you see pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through carefully to clear it. You should not speed up to beat the red light, and you must yield to pedestrians who are lawfully in the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Only inexperienced drivers are endangered by speed differences.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or make sudden lane changes and risky passing maneuvers. Safe driving means choosing a speed that is legal and appropriate for conditions, not simply going as slow as possible.

question: Which of these about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season,b:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe
note: Cruise control should not be used on snow, ice, or other slippery surfaces because it can cause your wheels to spin or lose traction before you can react. Winter is generally the most difficult driving season due to snow, ice, reduced visibility, and longer stopping distances, and checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important to keep the engine protected and the windshield clear.

question: What is the first thing you should adjust when getting into a car?
options: a:Your seat position so you can see and reach controls comfortably,b:Your rearview mirror,c:Your seat belt
note: You should adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals, steering wheel, and other controls comfortably and see clearly out of the windows. Once your seating position is correct, you then adjust your mirrors and finally fasten your seat belt before driving.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crash risk?
options: a:Just tell someone 'No thanks',b:Call a taxi only after you begin drinking,c:Decide before drinking that you will not drive
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive at all. Make a plan in advance—such as using a designated driver, taxi, or rideshare—because once you begin drinking, your judgment is impaired and you are more likely to make unsafe choices about driving.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Make every effort to get out of their way and avoid engaging them.,b:Stare at the driver to intimidate them.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and make every effort to move out of their way when it is safe. Do not speed up, brake‑check, or confront them, because that can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a crash.

question: Guide signs that show directions and distances are what color?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide or destination signs that show directions and distances are green with white lettering. They provide information such as route numbers, exits, and mileage to cities or destinations.

question: What is the most common color for general warning signs?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Most general warning signs in the U.S. are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering, which alerts drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what applies to turning vehicles?
options: a:You may still turn in the arrow's direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn at all.,c:You retain right-of-way to turn without yielding.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, but when it changes to a solid green light you must treat the turn as unprotected: you may turn in the arrow’s direction, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is illegal to drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:Driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic,b:You are in heavy construction zone traffic,c:Only when driving in rural areas
note: Driving significantly below the normal speed of traffic, without a good reason, can unlawfully impede or block traffic. You must not drive so slowly that you interfere with the normal, safe flow of vehicles.

question: What must a driver do at a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Merge to the right lane.,c:Accelerate through if no other cars are present.,d:Stop
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline where there is a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road ahead,b:Look straight ahead into the lights,c:Turn on and flash your high beams
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, you should avoid looking directly into the headlights. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare, helps you maintain your lane position, and prevents your eyes from being temporarily blinded.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop every time.,b:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,c:Speed up to get through first.,d:Leave at least one-half of the traveled portion of the road to the oncoming vehicle.
note: On narrow roads, you must share the roadway so that each vehicle has enough space to pass safely. The law generally requires that you leave at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road for oncoming traffic, rather than forcing the other driver off the road or trying to rush through first.

question: How can you reduce the need to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look far ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to warn others.,c:Drive in the leftmost lane only.
note: You can avoid many emergency stops by looking well ahead in traffic and keeping a safe following distance. Scanning the road gives you early warning of slowing or stopped vehicles, and extra space in front of you provides time to brake smoothly instead of stopping suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach an open (uncontrolled) intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who honks first,b:The driver on the left,c:The driver on the right
note: At an uncontrolled intersection—one without signs or signals—drivers who arrive at the same time must use the basic right-of-way rule: yield to the vehicle on your right. The driver on the left must let the driver on the right go first to prevent confusion and reduce the chance of a collision.

question: If you are angry after an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself while driving.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before starting your drive.,c:Drive fast to let off steam.,d:Immediately begin your commute to get home quicker.
note: Strong emotions like anger or frustration can distract you, slow your reactions, and lead to aggressive driving. If you are upset before driving, take a few minutes to calm down and regain your focus. Only start driving once you can concentrate fully on the road and make sound decisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to slow for a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.,b:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
note: On freeways, you should maintain the normal traffic speed until you are actually on the exit ramp, then slow down to the posted ramp speed. Braking early on the main freeway can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: When may you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Only in an emergency,b:If you turn on your hazard lights,c:If no part of your vehicle is on the road
note: Stopping or parking on a freeway shoulder is generally illegal except for true emergencies, such as a breakdown or medical problem. Hazard lights or being fully off the travel lane do not by themselves make shoulder parking legal if it is not an emergency.

question: If an oncoming car has its high beams on and blinds you, you should:
options: a:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs,b:Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes,c:Flash your lights at the oncoming driver
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s high beams blind you, avoid looking directly at the lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes, while keeping your lane position and speed under control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and exit the vehicle,c:Get your paperwork out and wave it at the officer
note: If stopped by law enforcement, stay in your vehicle unless directed otherwise, keep your hands clearly visible on the steering wheel, and wait for the officer’s instructions before reaching for your license, registration, or other documents.

question: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren, a driver must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and turn on four-way flashers,b:Pull to the right and slow down only,c:Pull to the right and stop
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and/or siren, you must move as close as safely possible to the right side of the road and come to a stop, remaining stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:Human error,c:New drivers
note: Across the U.S., the vast majority of crashes are caused by human error—such as inattention, speeding, following too closely, or poor judgment—not by weather or vehicle defects. While new drivers can make mistakes, experienced drivers also cause many crashes, so human error overall is the primary cause.

question: What do pennant-shaped roadside signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs that point to the left are used specifically for no-passing zones on two-lane roads. They warn you that you must not start or continue to pass in that area.

question: What must drivers do when approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Pass cautiously if no children appear to be present.,c:Sound the horn and pass on the left.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers must stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn and children are safely out of the roadway. In many states, this applies to traffic in both directions on undivided roads, but some states allow oncoming traffic to proceed on divided highways with a physical median. Always know your state’s specific rule, but never pass a bus with its stop arm out on your side of the road.

question: A downward-pointing triangular traffic sign indicates:
options: a:School zone,b:Construction zone,c:Yield to other traffic
note: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. It means you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and let cross traffic and pedestrians go first if they have the right-of-way.

question: Who is required by Indiana law to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:Only the driver.,b:Only occupants under age 18.,c:Only front-seat occupants.,d:All occupants of a vehicle equipped with seat belts.
note: Indiana is a primary seat belt law state: every person in a moving vehicle that has seat belts must wear one, regardless of seating position. Wearing seat belts greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Not cross the centerline at any time,b:Use the shoulder to pass if necessary,c:Move into the oncoming traffic lane only when it is safe and legal to do so
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you may pass a slower vehicle only by briefly moving into the oncoming lane when it is clearly safe and legal. Check for passing signs and road markings, make sure you have enough clear distance to pass without speeding, and return to your lane as soon as it is safe. Never use the shoulder or cross solid no-passing lines.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal,b:Apply the parking brake,c:Firmly pump the brake pedal
note: On a slippery road, the first step to slow down is to gently take your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle can slow without sudden weight shifts that cause skids. If you need to slow more, apply the brakes gently and steadily. Avoid hard braking or sudden pedal movements, which can lock the wheels and cause loss of control.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop,b:Ignore it if you don't see a train,c:Continue at the same speed unless gates are down
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, always slow down, look, and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop before the tracks, typically 15–50 feet away, and remain stopped until it is safe and legal to proceed.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement, what is the correct way to return to the road?
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately.,b:Slow down gradually,c:Turn the wheel sharply and jerk back onto the pavement.,d:Speed up and bounce back onto pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the wheel. Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually while keeping the vehicle straight. Once you have slowed and it is safe, gently steer back onto the pavement. Avoid slamming on the brakes or jerking the wheel, which can cause you to lose control or swerve into traffic.

question: What do round signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:School zones ahead.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round yellow signs are used specifically to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing. When you see this shape, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary. Other warnings, like school zones or no-passing zones, use different sign shapes.

question: What is required when you encounter an emergency vehicle using lights and sirens?
options: a:Speed up to pass the emergency vehicle.,b:Ignore the lights if you are in a hurry.,c:Yield the right-of-way and follow any instructions given by the emergency personnel.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and sirens, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right and stop if possible, and never block or try to outrun the vehicle. Follow any directions given by emergency personnel so they can pass quickly and safely.

question: What steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal as you begin the lane change without looking,b:Only check your blind spot by turning your head,c:Signal early, check mirrors, and check your blind spot
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move when the lane is clear and you can change lanes smoothly without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,b:Signal only when driving at night.,c:Always signal your intentions when changing lanes
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb, even if you think no one else is around. Signaling lets other road users know what you plan to do so they can adjust safely and avoid collisions.

question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection.,b:Ignore it if no other vehicles are present.,c:Slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection.,d:Speed up to get through before it turns red.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, continue through with caution instead of braking hard.

question: Which behavior best describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times,b:Looks for and anticipates the actions of other drivers,c:Travels at a constant speed
note: A good defensive driver stays alert, scans the road ahead, and anticipates what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do. By expecting possible mistakes from others and leaving space and time to react, defensive drivers reduce the risk of collisions.

question: When driving in fog, which actions improve safety?
options: a:Do not use your high beam headlights.,b:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.,c:All of the above.,d:Use low beam headlights to better see the road ahead.
note: In fog, visibility is reduced and light reflects off the water droplets. Use low beam headlights, not high beams, because high beams can create glare and make it harder to see. Slow down and drive cautiously so you have more time to react to hazards you may not see until you are close.

question: At a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Stop only if a train is visible.,b:Cross immediately to avoid delays.,c:Prepare to yield to any approaching train and never cross unless you can see clearly that all tracks are clear.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, you must approach with caution, slow or stop if needed, and look and listen carefully for trains in both directions. Never start across unless you can clearly see that all tracks are clear and there is enough room to fully clear the tracks without stopping.

question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Ignore traffic around you if mirrors look clear.,b:Change lanes without signaling to be faster.,c:Check side and rearview mirrors, signal, and check your blind spot before changing lanes.
note: When changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. Mirrors alone do not show everything around your vehicle, so a head check is essential to be sure the lane is clear and it is safe to move.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You must come to a complete stop before turning,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You should merge into the lane of the arrow first
note: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means you may turn left, but only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Oncoming vehicles and people in the crosswalk have the right-of-way, and you must wait for a safe gap before turning.

question: When are roads most slippery after rain begins?
options: a:The day after it rains.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm because oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the water and rise to the top. After it has rained for a while, much of this washes away and traction usually improves, though you should still drive carefully.

question: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means:
options: a:A stop sign,b:A hospital sign,c:A speed limit sign
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign shape is used only for STOP signs in the U.S. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact
note: With an aggressive driver, your goal is to avoid escalating the situation. Do not retaliate, race, or make gestures. Avoid eye contact, stay calm, create space between your vehicle and theirs, and if needed, change routes or contact authorities from a safe location.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to clear the street.,b:Slow down but continue through the intersection.,c:Pull safely to the right curb and stop until you can locate the vehicle.,d:Keep driving until you actually see it.
note: When you hear a siren, you must yield the right-of-way to the emergency vehicle, even if you cannot see it yet. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop, then locate the vehicle and remain stopped until it has passed and it is safe to re-enter traffic.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign typically:
options: a:Alerts you to school zones,b:Indicates public recreation areas,c:Warns of existing or possible hazards ahead
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to existing or possible hazards such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or changes in road conditions so you can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:High speeds.,c:Clear weather.,d:Night driving only.
note: Higher speeds make it take much longer to stop because both your reaction distance and braking distance increase. Speed also increases the force of a crash, so collisions at high speed are much more severe and more likely to cause serious injury or death.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Passengers when they are on long trips,b:All occupants of the vehicle,c:The person driving the car only
note: Seat belts are most effective when every person in the vehicle wears one, regardless of where they are sitting or how long the trip is. In a crash, unbelted passengers can be thrown around inside the vehicle or ejected, and they can also strike and seriously injure belted occupants. For maximum safety, all occupants should always wear seat belts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Speed up and go first.,c:Ignore it and drive through.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and let the vehicle on your right go first.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Keep the same following distance as in dry conditions.,b:Roads are often most slippery soon after rain begins,c:Turn off your headlights to prevent glare.,d:Wet roads never cause hydroplaning.
note: When rain first begins, oil and debris on the road mix with the water and make the surface especially slippery. Reduce your speed and increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react and to help prevent skidding or hydroplaning.

question: If you hear a siren from behind while on the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are without signaling.,b:Speed up to get out of the way.,c:Safely pull over to the right and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.,d:Turn into the opposing lane to clear a path.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind, you must safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. Use your signals, check mirrors and blind spots, and avoid stopping in an intersection. In heavy traffic, move as far right as you safely can to create a clear path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed to the next exit and return on surface streets to your destination.,b:Make a U-turn across the median.,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,d:Stop and ask another driver for help.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, continue to the next exit. Once off the freeway, you can safely turn around using surface streets or re‑enter the freeway in the opposite direction if needed. Never back up on the freeway or drive across the median, as these actions are extremely dangerous and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn when you reach an intersection, you should go straight, continue to the next intersection, and then make your turn from the proper lane. Sudden lane changes or turns from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause crashes.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:Alcohol always helps the medicine work better.,b:The medicine will cancel out the alcohol.,c:The combination can multiply the effects and increase impairment.
note: Alcohol can interact with both prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines in ways that increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment. The combination can multiply the effects of each substance, making it much more dangerous to drive than using either one alone.

question: What type of sign warns drivers about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Warning signs,b:Regulatory signs,c:Information signs
note: Warning signs are typically yellow with black symbols or words and are used to alert drivers to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. They give you time to slow down or adjust your driving for safety.

question: What can result when alcohol is consumed together with other drugs?
options: a:They have no additional effect.,b:They always cancel each other out.,c:They make you sober faster.,d:The combined effects can increase impairment and be more dangerous than either alone.
note: When alcohol is combined with other drugs—whether legal or illegal—the effects on the brain and body can be intensified. This can greatly increase impairment of judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving far more dangerous than using either substance alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left if two arrive at once.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The driver who arrived first.
note: At a four‑way stop, the driver who arrives first has the right‑of‑way and should proceed first after stopping. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. These rules help keep traffic moving safely and predictably.

question: The impairment caused by lack of sleep is most like the impairment from:
options: a:Alcohol,b:Amphetamines,c:Anger
note: Fatigue affects judgment, reaction time, and coordination in a way that is very similar to alcohol. After many hours awake, drivers can be as impaired as if they had a moderate blood alcohol concentration, so lack of sleep is most like alcohol impairment.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as:
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way.

question: What colors identify signs that show distance to upcoming highway exits?
options: a:Green with white letters,b:Yellow with black letters,c:Red with white letters
note: Highway guide signs that show directions, destinations, and distances are typically green with white letters or symbols. These signs help drivers locate exits and measure how far they are from upcoming locations.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio reliably prevents drowsiness,b:Drowsy drivers can perform as poorly as drunk drivers and may appear intoxicated,c:Drinking strong coffee permanently restores full alertness
note: Drowsy drivers can be as dangerous as drunk drivers. Fatigue slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and can cause lane drifting or poor judgment that may look like intoxication. Quick tricks like opening a window or drinking coffee do not reliably or permanently restore safe alertness.

question: A person walking with a white cane or using a guide dog is usually:
options: a:Part of a traffic study.,b:A traffic enforcement officer.,c:A blind or visually impaired pedestrian.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is usually blind or visually impaired. Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way to these pedestrians and use extra caution, allowing them plenty of time and space to cross safely.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing tracks that has no signals or gates, what should you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way so proceed regardless.,b:Make sure there is space ahead for your vehicle to clear the tracks without stopping.,c:You may stop on the tracks if necessary.,d:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.
note: Before you drive onto railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks without stopping. Never enter a crossing if traffic ahead might force you to stop on the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal behavior corresponds to stopping, yielding, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid green light
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when it is safe, just like at a stop sign.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only if no oncoming traffic is present.,b:Yes,c:No — you may not cross a double solid yellow line to pass
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is not allowed in either direction. You may cross it only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when specifically allowed by law, but not to pass another moving vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Is not required to stop.,b:Stop at the point nearest the intersection where you can see approaching traffic without entering the roadway.,c:Is required to slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
note: If you must stop at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point just before entering the intersecting roadway where you can best see approaching traffic, without actually moving into the intersection.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are only found in construction zones.,b:Provide information for drivers.,c:Are usually not important.
note: Highway pavement markings give important information such as lane use, where passing is allowed, where to stop, and how traffic flows. Drivers must understand and follow these markings to drive safely.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Always come to a full stop.,c:Slow and yield to vehicles or pedestrians; be prepared to stop.
note: A red-and-white triangle is a yield sign. You must slow down, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop if traffic or pedestrians are close enough to be a hazard, but you do not have to stop if the way is clear.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings must be treated how by drivers?
options: a:Must always be obeyed.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls, not suggestions. Drivers must obey them at all times unless a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic differently.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages while on a public road or highway?
options: a:Only if you are not driving.,b:Never — consuming or possessing open alcohol in areas of the vehicle normally occupied by people on a public road is generally prohibited.,c:Only if you are seated in the back of a vehicle.
note: Open container laws generally prohibit having open alcoholic beverages in areas of a vehicle normally occupied by the driver or passengers on public roads. In many states, including Indiana, it is illegal to consume alcohol or have an open container in these areas while on a public roadway, regardless of whether you are the driver or a passenger.

question: A load that extends more than how far beyond a vehicle's rear must be flagged during daylight?
options: a:One foot,b:Two feet,c:Four feet
note: If a load extends more than 4 feet beyond the rear of a vehicle, it must be clearly marked in daylight with a red flag that is at least 12 inches square so other drivers can see the overhanging load in time to react safely.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed only when safe.,b:Slow down but do not stop.,c:Proceed with caution without stopping.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely at the intersection, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the road is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic if there is no gap.,b:Assume they have the right-of-way.,c:Signal only after entering the road.,d:Yield to drivers already on the public road.
note: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the roadway. Wait for a safe gap, signal, and merge only when you can do so without forcing other drivers to slow or change lanes suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a red light you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield to pedestrians and cross traffic before turning,b:Honk at nearby pedestrians before turning,c:Turn without stopping if the lane is clear
note: To turn right on red (where allowed), you must first come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk, check for and yield to pedestrians and all cross traffic, and only turn when it is safe and not prohibited by signs.

question: Regarding small children riding in vehicles, which is correct?
options: a:They may be safely held by a strong adult,b:They may stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle,c:They must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint or safety seat
note: Small children must always be secured in an approved child safety seat or restraint that is appropriate for their size and age. Holding a child or allowing them to stand is extremely dangerous because even low‑speed crashes can throw them from an adult’s arms.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance must you signal before making a turn in most situations?
options: a:350 feet,b:At least 100–200 feet (follow your state’s specific requirement),c:120 yards
note: In many states you must signal at least 100 feet before turning, and some require 200 feet or more. The key rule is to signal well in advance so other drivers and pedestrians clearly understand your intentions before you slow or turn.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:All of the above,b:Only body weight,c:Only the amount of food in the stomach
note: Alcohol’s effect depends on several factors, including how much you drink, how quickly you drink, your body weight, and whether you have food in your stomach. These factors change how quickly alcohol enters your bloodstream and how impaired you become.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to turn green.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means the signal is warning you to use extra caution. You do not need to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or hazards, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left,b:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right
note: At a four-way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps avoid confusion and collisions at intersections without signals.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Turn on your car radio,b:Slow down,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch
note: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, plan to stop regularly to get out, walk, and stretch. Short breaks help restore alertness much more effectively than just turning on the radio or slowing down, which do not prevent fatigue.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do to warn other drivers?
options: a:Use only parking lights.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,c:Use your emergency flashers and keep low-beam headlights on.,d:Stand behind your vehicle with a flashlight.
note: If you must stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low‑beam headlights on so other drivers can see your vehicle from a distance. Making your vehicle clearly visible reduces the risk of being hit by approaching traffic.

question: What is the legal status of texting while driving in Indiana?
options: a:It is legal only when stopped at a light.,b:It is allowed for drivers over 21.,c:It is illegal to type or read a text or email while driving,d:It is always legal.
note: In Indiana, it is illegal to type, transmit, or read text or email messages while driving. This law is meant to reduce distracted driving crashes; only limited emergency use may be allowed under specific circumstances.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It causes immediate engine failure,b:It causes your tires to wear faster,c:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger area leading to poisoning
note: A leaking exhaust can let carbon monoxide enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless, and breathing it can quickly cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death. Because you may not notice it, any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are drivers required to stop?
options: a:When a traffic officer or flagger orders you to stop,b:At red lights and flashing red lights,c:At stop signs, red or flashing red lights, and when directed by a traffic officer or flagger
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at red lights and flashing red lights, and whenever a traffic officer or flagger directs you to stop. Stopping is required any time a traffic control device or authorized person indicates that you must yield the right‑of‑way and come to a full stop before proceeding safely.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before changing lanes called?
options: a:An unnecessary action,b:A bad driving habit,c:A good driving habit
note: Turning your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes is a good and necessary driving habit. Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, so a quick glance over your shoulder helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians that might be hidden in those blind spots.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that may affect safety, what should you do?
options: a:Drive slower until you can fix it.,b:Wait until you can afford it.,c:Have it repaired as soon as possible.
note: Any defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle should be repaired as soon as possible, and the vehicle should not be driven if the defect makes it unsafe. Problems with brakes, steering, tires, lights, or other critical systems can lead to loss of control or crashes if not corrected promptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, what should you remember?
options: a:You are always allowed to pass on the uphill.,b:The truck will be going the posted speed.,c:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Heavy trucks often climb hills much more slowly than the posted speed limit because of their size and weight. When you approach a truck from behind on an uphill, expect it to be moving slowly, increase your following distance, and only pass when it is legal, safe, and you have enough clear distance to complete the maneuver.

question: A pentagonal (five-sided) sign indicates:
options: a:No passing zone,b:A school zone or school crossing,c:Speed limits ahead
note: A pentagonal (five‑sided) sign is used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians or crossing guards.

question: Which color is commonly used for signs marking public recreation or cultural areas?
options: a:Brown,b:Red,c:Green
note: Brown signs indicate public recreation areas, parks, and cultural or historic points of interest. They help drivers locate places like campgrounds, museums, and scenic sites.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
note: To begin parallel parking, first pull up alongside and even with the car in front of the space, leaving a safe gap. Then you shift to reverse and turn the wheel as you back into the space.

question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling,b:Activate your turn signal three to four seconds in advance,c:Increase your speed before turning
note: Before turning, signal at least several seconds in advance so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions. This gives them time to adjust and helps prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal after changing lanes.,b:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.,c:Signal just before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.
note: When passing, signal early enough so other drivers clearly see you intend to change lanes. This advance warning lets them adjust speed or position and reduces the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,b:Changing lanes.,c:All of the above.
note: You must always signal before changing lanes or entering traffic, and when pulling into or out of a parking space or alley. Signaling lets other drivers and pedestrians know your intentions so they can react safely.

question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:High beam headlights,c:Parking lights only
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder for you and others to see. Parking lights alone are not sufficient and are generally illegal to use as driving lights.

question: If you are involved in a crash, you should:
options: a:Leave the scene immediately to avoid trouble,b:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene and render aid as needed,c:Stand in traffic lanes to direct other drivers
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, check for injuries, call for help if needed, and provide reasonable assistance. If vehicles can be moved and there are no serious injuries, move them out of traffic to prevent another collision. Never leave the scene or stand in active traffic lanes.

question: You should sound your horn when you:
options: a:Are traveling through an intersection with a green light,b:See a child about to run into the street,c:Are passing a bicyclist in a residential area
note: Use your horn to warn others when there is an immediate risk of a collision, such as when a child is about to run into the street or another driver is about to hit you. Do not use the horn unnecessarily, such as when you simply have a green light or when passing a bicyclist unless they appear unaware of your presence and a warning is needed for safety.

question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving in your lane,b:Pull to the right curb and stop,c:Slow down and continue
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.,b:Drive faster to get your mind off things.,c:Assume emotions won't affect your driving.
note: Strong emotions like anger, fear, or crying can seriously reduce your concentration, judgment, and reaction time. You should not drive until you have calmed down and can focus fully on the road. Take a break, breathe, and wait until you feel in control before starting to drive.

question: Which factor directly affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The color of surrounding vehicles.,b:The number of passengers in other cars.,c:The condition of the road surface.
note: Stopping distance depends on traction between your tires and the road. Wet, icy, snowy, or gravel surfaces greatly increase the distance it takes to stop. When the road surface is poor, you must slow down and increase following distance so you can stop safely.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a standard crossbuck and no gates or lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Turn down your radio to hear better and drive through quickly.,b:Cross immediately if you don’t see a train,c:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when sure no train is coming.,d:Speed up to clear the tracks faster.
note: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no lights or gates, you must treat it with extra caution. Slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, be prepared to stop, and only cross when you are absolutely sure no train is coming and there is enough room to clear the tracks completely.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Shift to neutral, apply the brakes as needed, carefully turn off the ignition to stop the engine, and move off the road to a safe location.,b:Brake hard and immediately open the hood while moving.,c:Keep driving until you reach a service station.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep calm and stay in control. Shift to neutral to disconnect the engine from the wheels, apply firm, steady brakes, and steer carefully. Once you are in control, turn off the ignition without locking the steering, and move off the road to a safe place to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at a green light but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection instead.,b:Wait behind the stop line until the light turns yellow.,c:Enter the intersection and wait there until oncoming traffic clears, then turn when it is safe.
note: With a green light and no green arrow, oncoming traffic has the right of way. You may pull into the intersection and wait with your wheels straight until there is a safe gap. When oncoming traffic clears or the light turns yellow/red and opposing traffic stops, complete your left turn quickly and safely.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, stay calm, and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not slam on the brakes, because that can cause you to lose control. Instead, ease off the accelerator so the car slows down gradually, signal, and carefully steer to the side of the road when it is safe. Once stopped, turn on your hazard lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights to ask for a gap in traffic,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight,c:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Signal your turn, keep the wheels straight, and only turn the wheel left as you actually begin the turn when it is safe and clear.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign ahead, you should:
options: a:Try to drive around any lowered gates,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby,c:Speed up to cross before the train arrives
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching train tracks and must be ready to stop. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching. Never drive around lowered gates or ignore warning lights or bells, because trains cannot stop quickly and a collision is often fatal.

question: When the traffic light turns from green to a solid yellow as you approach, you should:
options: a:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.,b:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,c:Speed up to beat the light.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you can stop safely before entering the intersection, you must do so. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution rather than braking hard at the last moment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the freeway you see a \Merging traffic\" sign. You should:"
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over a lane if safe,b:Maintain your current speed regardless,c:Always honk at incoming traffic
note: A merging traffic sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane from an on‑ramp or side road. You should help traffic merge smoothly by adjusting your speed and, if possible and safe, moving over to the next lane to create space.
