Do not block merging vehicles or maintain speed in a way that prevents them from entering safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit or safe location to turn around,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder,c:Make the turn quickly from your current lane
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit or another safe place to turn around. Never stop, back up, or make a sudden turn across lanes on the freeway, because traffic is moving fast and unexpected maneuvers can cause serious crashes.

question: What should you do before driving in an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Plan your trip in advance,b:Rely solely on road signs to find your way,c:Only have a general idea of your destination
note: Before driving in an unfamiliar area, review a map, GPS route, or directions so you know your main turns and highways ahead of time. Planning reduces last‑second lane changes and distractions from trying to navigate only by reading signs while you are already driving.

question: During the first 180 days after receiving a probationary license, which restriction commonly applies?
options: a:May be subject to nighttime driving restrictions, depending on state law.,b:May not drive between 10:00 pm and 5:00 am in all states.,c:May not transport any passengers in all states.
note: Many states place night‑driving and passenger limits on new drivers, but the exact hours and rules vary by state. Some states restrict driving after midnight, others use different curfew windows, and some focus more on passenger limits than specific times. Always check your own state’s graduated licensing rules for the exact curfew and passenger restrictions during the first months of a probationary or intermediate license.

question: What is the safe way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass,b:Honk to alert the bicyclist,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and leave plenty of space—many states require at least 3 feet or more. Wait until it is safe, move well into the adjacent lane if possible, and never drive in the bike lane or crowd the rider. Avoid honking close to the bicyclist, as it can startle them and cause a loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A green arrow pointing left.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A solid green light.
note: A green left‑turn arrow means you have a protected turn: oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing a red light must stop, so you may turn left when the intersection is clear. A solid green light does not give you the right‑of‑way to turn left; you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: What should drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They can stop faster than passenger vehicles,b:They need less space to turn than smaller cars,c:They have large blind spots and need more room to stop and maneuver
note: Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than passenger cars and need more distance to stop and more space to turn or change lanes. Because of their size and weight, they cannot stop or maneuver as quickly as smaller vehicles, so drivers should give them extra space.

question: When may you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights have stopped flashing,b:When the train has passed,c:Under no circumstances
note: You must never drive around or under lowered gates at a railroad crossing, even if you do not see a train. Trains are large, fast, and cannot stop quickly, and signals may activate before you can see the train. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and signals indicate it is safe to proceed.

question: How can alcoholic beverages affect a driver?
options: a:They only affect very inexperienced drivers.,b:They improve coordination.,c:They can slow reaction time
note: Alcohol affects all drivers by slowing reaction time, reducing coordination, and impairing judgment and vision. Even small amounts can make it harder to respond quickly to hazards, increasing the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed if clear,b:Stop only if pedestrians are present,c:Stop before entering the intersection
note: A steady red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or entering the intersection. You must remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic with the right-of-way.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
note: When parking downhill on a two-way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will rest against the curb and help prevent it from rolling into traffic.

question: What should you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,b:Proceed through carefully after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means proceed with caution, not stop. You must slow down, scan for other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over the others?
options: a:A steady red traffic light,b:A police officer directing traffic,c:A stop sign
note: Instructions from a police officer or authorized traffic controller override traffic lights and signs. If an officer’s directions conflict with signals or signs, you must follow the officer for safety and traffic control.

question: What is the only effective method to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee,b:Exercise,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol; coffee, exercise, or cold showers may make you feel more awake but do not make you less impaired or reduce BAC.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Whenever you see a bus regardless of lights,b:When the bus is stopped with red lights flashing and loading/unloading children,c:Only when the bus is parked on the shoulder
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and/or its stop arm extended while children are getting on or off. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn to warn kids.,b:Ignore it if there are no children visible.,c:Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, watch carefully for children who may enter the street unexpectedly, and be prepared to stop if needed.

question: How can a person sober up quickly after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee will remove the effects of alcohol.,b:Drinking tomato juice and lime will sober them up.,c:Only the passage of time will reduce the effects of alcohol; coffee or fresh air will not sober you up.,d:Fresh air instantly cancels alcohol impairment.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, food, cold showers, or fresh air might make you feel more awake, but they do not make you less impaired or safe to drive. Your body needs time to process and eliminate the alcohol.

question: How do blind spots of larger vehicles compare to smaller vehicles?
options: a:Larger vehicles have no blind spots,b:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots,c:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots
note: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have much bigger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly in front, along both sides, and behind the vehicle. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you, so avoid lingering in those areas.

question: May you drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate,b:Only if an approaching train is not too close,c:You must never drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a lowered or lowering railroad gate. Trains are fast, heavy, and cannot stop quickly. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning lights and bells have stopped before crossing.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, when should you allow a larger space cushion in front of you?
options: a:Never; keep the same spacing.,b:When stopped on an incline so the vehicle ahead cannot roll back into you.,c:Only at stop signs.,d:Only at traffic signals.
note: On an uphill slope, leave extra space in front of you when stopped. The vehicle ahead may roll backward when the driver moves from the brake to the accelerator, and a larger space cushion helps you avoid a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do with your speed when making a turn?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control and stay in your lane,b:Increase your speed,c:Maintain your previous speed
note: Before entering a turn, slow down to a safe speed so you can stay in your lane and maintain control. Turning at high speed increases the risk of skidding, drifting out of your lane, or losing control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it not permitted to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When you want to pass a motorcycle.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:If doing so would interfere with traffic or be unsafe.,d:When the car ahead is disabled.
note: A single broken white or yellow line means you may cross it to change lanes or pass, but only when it is safe and will not interfere with other traffic. If crossing the line would force other drivers to brake or swerve, or if visibility or road conditions make it unsafe, you must not cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with two solid yellow centerlines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway,b:To pass if no oncoming traffic is visible,c:Never under any circumstances
note: Two solid yellow centerlines mean no passing from either direction. However, you may carefully cross them to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway when it is legal and safe. You may not cross them just to pass another vehicle.

question: What do work zone signs indicate to drivers?
options: a:That it is summer,b:You must stop and back up immediately,c:Less-than-ideal driving conditions ahead
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work or construction is ahead. They alert you to changing traffic patterns, workers and equipment near the roadway, and other less-than-ideal driving conditions, so you should slow down and use extra caution.

question: When passing a large truck, a smaller vehicle should be prepared for:
options: a:Excess air pollution,b:Sudden wind gusts from the large vehicle,c:Loud noises
note: When passing a large truck or bus, the air turbulence and wind gusts around the vehicle can push or pull a smaller vehicle sideways. You should hold the steering wheel firmly and be prepared to make small steering corrections as you move past and clear the truck.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer vs. wine vs. liquor) change its effect on reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Wine impairs less than beer,b:Beer impairs less than wine,c:No — alcohol's effects depend on blood alcohol concentration
note: Alcohol’s effect on your reflexes and judgment depends on how much pure alcohol you have in your system, measured as blood alcohol concentration (BAC), not on whether it came from beer, wine, or liquor. A standard serving of each has about the same amount of alcohol and can impair you equally.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Certain prescription or over-the-counter medications.,c:A lack of sleep.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol, many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, and being very tired all slow your reactions and hurt your judgment and coordination. Any of these can make it unsafe to drive, so you must be cautious and avoid driving when you are impaired for any reason.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.,b:Pedestrians in the roundabout only.,c:Bicyclists in the roundabout only.,d:Vehicles in the roundabout only.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to all traffic already in the circle, including vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Enter only when there is a safe gap so you do not force others to slow or stop.

question: Why is driving at night generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark,c:It usually rains more at night.,d:Headlights are brighter at night.
note: At night you cannot see as far or as clearly, even with headlights. Reduced visibility makes it harder to spot hazards, judge distances, and see pedestrians or animals, so you should slow down and use proper lighting to match how far you can see.

question: On a divided multilane highway, if you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right side of the road and stop if possible.,b:Slow down,c:Stop immediately in your travel lane.,d:Speed up to stay ahead.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping, if possible, until it passes. On a divided multilane highway, you still slow and move right; do not speed up or stop in the middle of your lane unless traffic or the divider makes pulling over impossible.

question: Which is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than normal traffic only,b:Weaving between lanes,c:Making quick and sudden stops only,d:All of the above
note: A common sign of an impaired driver is weaving or drifting between lanes, which shows poor control and judgment. Other signs can include driving much too slowly or too fast, sudden stops, and inconsistent speed, but weaving is one of the clearest warning signs.

question: What is the 'No zone' with respect to large trucks and buses?
options: a:A speed-restricted zone.,b:A noise restriction area.,c:The large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from view.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots directly in front, directly behind, and along both sides. These areas are called the 'No-Zone' because the driver may not see you there. Staying out of these blind spots gives the truck or bus driver more time and space to react and reduces your risk of a collision.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do immediately for safety?
options: a:Signal, exit the roadway carefully, use hazard flashers, and park where other drivers can see you.,b:Sit in the car and wait with the engine running.,c:Sound your horn to attract attention.,d:Stand behind your vehicle facing traffic.
note: If your car breaks down on a highway, first signal and carefully move off the roadway to the shoulder or a safe area where other drivers can see you. Turn on your hazard flashers so approaching traffic knows your vehicle is disabled. If it is safe, you may raise the hood to make the vehicle more visible, but your top priority is getting out of the traffic lane and making your vehicle clearly visible to others.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect on either,b:It harms both driving skills and judgement,c:It helps driving skills but harms judgement
note: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, narrows your field of vision, and impairs judgment and decision‑making. Even small amounts make it harder to steer, brake, stay in your lane, and respond to hazards. Because it harms both your driving skills and your judgment, you should never drive after drinking.

question: What is highway hypnosis and how does it occur?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
note: Highway hypnosis is a trance‑like state that can occur when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods without actively scanning. Your mind drifts, you may not remember the last few miles, and you react more slowly to hazards. To prevent it, take regular breaks, keep your eyes moving, and avoid driving when tired.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect performance?
options: a:It has no effect on driving ability,b:It improves concentration so drivers make fewer errors,c:It increases the chance of driving errors and difficulty controlling the vehicle
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and your eyes and attention off the road. This increases the chance of drifting out of your lane, missing traffic signals, or failing to see hazards in time. Any activity that divides your attention from driving raises the risk of errors and crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstance may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is adequate room to pass.,b:When it requires driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn and there is enough space in a clearly marked lane to pass safely without leaving the paved roadway. It is illegal and unsafe to pass on the right by driving off the pavement or onto the shoulder.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is:
options: a:Helpful to maintain driver alertness,b:A distracting activity,c:Not affecting driving abilities
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. Any activity that diverts your focus, hands, or eyes from driving increases your risk of a crash and should be avoided while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The right lane,b:Either lane as you choose,c:The lane closest to your previous lane
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, you must turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from. This keeps traffic organized and prevents you from cutting across lanes, which could cause conflicts with vehicles already on the one-way street.

question: What does a posted advisory or speed restriction sign typically indicate?
options: a:Shows an advisory speed for curves and turns.,b:Is triangular in shape.,c:Is blue with black lettering.
note: Advisory or speed restriction signs show a recommended safe speed for specific conditions such as curves, ramps, or turns. They are not the absolute speed limit, but you should slow to at least that speed, and even more in bad weather or poor visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes?
options: a:You should always use cruise control.,b:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,c:Signal
note: Before changing lanes on an interstate, you must signal to let other drivers know your intention, then check your mirrors and blind spots and move only when it is safe. Cruise control is optional and the shoulder is for emergencies, not for routine lane changes or rest stops.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem indicate?
options: a:The vehicle must yield to all traffic.,b:The vehicle is designed to travel at 25 mph or slower and will display a reflective orange triangle.,c:The vehicle is a commercial vehicle.,d:The vehicle should be passed only on the left.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border mounted on the rear of vehicles designed to travel at 25 mph or less. When you see this emblem, expect the vehicle to be moving much more slowly than normal traffic and be prepared to slow down and pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: Which is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter the curve and brake while exiting.,b:Slow down before entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,c:Maintain a constant speed through the entire curve.
note: Before entering a curve, you should slow down so your vehicle is under control and your tires maintain good traction. Once you are safely in the curve and can see the road ahead, you may gradually accelerate as you exit. Braking hard in a curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on wet or slippery roads.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They always break the law.,c:They must always yield to cars.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden easily in traffic, blind spots, or by larger vehicles. Because they are harder to see and more vulnerable in a crash, drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield when required to help prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A good rule to follow regarding passing other vehicles is:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary.,b:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to see better.,c:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: A safe passing rule is to drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and pass only when it is necessary and legal. Passing always carries extra risk because you move into another lane and may face oncoming traffic. You should never routinely try to get to the front of traffic, and you should pass on the right only in limited situations specifically allowed by law, not "whenever possible."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you find yourself stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stop to look up an address in the travel lane.,b:Drop off passengers in the travel lane.,c:Move out of the travel lane as soon as you can to a safe location; do not stop in a travel lane.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane except in emergencies. If your vehicle is moving, continue until you can safely pull off the roadway to the shoulder or a designated parking area. Stopping in a travel lane to look for an address or drop off passengers creates a serious hazard and increases the risk of rear-end collisions.

question: If you are being tailgated, what should you do if you cannot change lanes?
options: a:Speed up aggressively to put distance between you.,b:Wait until the road ahead is clear and then reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Brake abruptly to warn the tailgater.,d:Honk continuously to make them back off.
note: If you are being tailgated and cannot safely change lanes, create more space in front of your vehicle and gradually slow down when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass you without sudden braking that could cause a rear‑end collision. Avoid brake‑checking, honking aggressively, or speeding up, as these actions increase risk.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas to slow and apply brakes smoothly,b:Always check mirrors and blind spots before stopping but stop abruptly when necessary,c:Tap your brakes repeatedly to warn the following driver,d:Leave extra following distance so you can slow gradually if traffic ahead stops
note: To help prevent rear‑end collisions, look well ahead, ease off the accelerator early, and apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. This gives drivers behind you more time to react and stop safely. Sudden or unnecessary hard braking increases the chance that a following driver will not be able to stop in time.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Yield only to vehicles from the left.,b:Continue normally without slowing.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.,d:Slow down and proceed with care.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You must slow down, scan the intersection, and continue only when it is safe. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what is required?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then turn when safe.,b:Maintain normal speed and turn without stopping.,c:Stop and look for police cars before turning.,d:Turn immediately without checking cross traffic.
note: When turning right on a green light, you may proceed without stopping if the way is clear, but you must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or entering the intersection. Turning only when it is safe prevents conflicts with crossing traffic and people on foot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:May honk your horn, but still must yield to traffic and pedestrians before entering.,b:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,c:Must drive slowly but still yield to all pedestrians and approaching vehicles before entering the street.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or curb line and yield to pedestrians and all approaching traffic on the roadway. Do not rely on your horn or expect others to move for you; you are responsible for entering only when it is safe.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Pass with caution,b:Slow down immediately,c:Do not pass from your lane
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass from your lane. It indicates that visibility or conditions ahead are unsafe for passing, so you must stay in your lane until the marking changes or the restriction ends.

question: To check your blind spot when moving left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: When moving left, you must check the blind spot on the left side of your vehicle by quickly glancing over your left shoulder. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in your blind spot, so this shoulder check helps ensure the lane is clear before you move over.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Continue without changing speed.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop because the light will soon turn red.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, proceed with caution through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Quickly cut across lanes to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and exit there rather than making a last-minute maneuver.
note: If you miss your exit on the interstate, stay calm and continue to the next exit. Never make a U-turn across the median or swerve across lanes at the last second, as these maneuvers are illegal and extremely dangerous at highway speeds.

question: Which of these does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:The condition of your brakes.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance is made up of your reaction distance and your braking distance. It is affected by your reaction time, the condition of your brakes and tires, your speed, and road conditions. The time of day by itself does not change how far it takes your vehicle to stop.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow the directions of the crossing guard,b:Ignore the guard and follow surrounding traffic,c:Assume the guard has no authority
note: Crossing guards have legal authority in school zones. You must follow their hand signals and instructions, even if they differ from traffic lights or what other drivers are doing. Always slow down, be prepared to stop, and watch carefully for children.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Get off highways as quickly as possible,b:Reduce speed and increase following distance,c:Add extra weight to the vehicle for traction
note: On snow or ice, the most important safety steps are to slow down and leave a much larger following distance. This gives you more time to react and more space to stop on the slippery surface. Sudden steering, braking, or acceleration should be avoided.

question: To prevent your physical condition from making you an unsafe driver, which of the following should you prioritize?
options: a:Drive within your physical limitations.,b:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,c:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,d:All of the above.
note: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. You should drive only within your physical limits, understand how any medications you take can affect alertness and coordination, and maintain your health with regular checkups. All of these together help prevent your condition from making you an unsafe driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green arrow on a traffic signal allow you to do?
options: a:Should slow to a stop.,b:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,c:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
note: A steady green arrow means you are allowed to make the turn in the direction of the arrow. This is a protected turn, but you must still yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk and to vehicles already in the intersection before you turn.

question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Speed up to increase distance from them.,b:Slam on your brakes to warn them.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: When someone is following too closely, the safest response is to let them pass. If possible, change lanes, or gradually slow down to encourage them to go around you. Avoid speeding up or braking suddenly, as these can increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To whom must drivers yield?
options: a:Only pedestrians on the same side of the road.,b:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,c:Pedestrians only when they have a green signal.,d:Pedestrians in the roadway
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are in the roadway, whether they are in a marked crosswalk, an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection, or otherwise legally crossing. Even if a pedestrian is crossing unexpectedly or against a signal, you must slow or stop as needed to avoid hitting them.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
options: a:Same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe,b:The traffic signal is broken and you may proceed without stopping,c:You do not have to stop completely
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians and other vehicles that have the right-of-way, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate:
options: a:Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill,b:Passing is not allowed,c:Passing is allowed for drivers in both directions
note: Two solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions mean that passing is not allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction. You may cross these lines only when making a left turn or when allowed by specific signs or markings, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: Which of the following is true about railroad crossings?
options: a:Flaggers cannot direct vehicles at crossings.,b:It is illegal to go around lowered gates,c:All railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.,d:You may always go around lowered gates if traffic is light.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. You must obey all warning devices and any flagger’s directions, and only proceed once the gates are fully raised and the tracks are clear.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Directions to cities and towns,b:Traffic laws and regulations,c:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead
note: Yellow-and-black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width or surface.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A speed limit sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn, what should drivers do?
options: a:Signal in advance, watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and move into the left lane when appropriate.,b:Speed up and turn sharply.,c:Ignore pedestrians if you have the green.,d:Signal only after starting the turn.
note: Before a left turn, signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, move into the proper left lane when allowed, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A single dashed yellow centerline means:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so,b:Drivers may not pass,c:Both lanes travel in the same direction
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing when it can be done safely and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

question: Faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what is the safest course?
options: a:Try to split the difference and squeeze between both hazards.,b:Honk and speed up to get by quickly.,c:Pull onto the shoulder immediately.,d:Let the oncoming car pass
note: When facing an oncoming vehicle and a bicyclist at the same time, deal with one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, then move over safely to give the bicyclist plenty of space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What problem does driving much slower than the posted speed often create?
options: a:It guarantees you the right-of-way,b:You should never allow following cars to pass,c:It can be hazardous and may require you to pull off to let traffic pass
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can create a hazard by causing sudden braking and lane changes. On many two-lane roads, if you are holding up traffic, you are required to pull off where safe and let vehicles pass.

question: What danger can a leaking exhaust system pose to occupants?
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning that can cause drowsiness or death,b:Excessive oil consumption,c:Need for more frequent tune-ups
note: A leaking exhaust can let carbon monoxide and other fumes enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can cause headache, dizziness, drowsiness, and eventually death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately and the vehicle ventilated.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, what should you do after a train passes?
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.,b:Immediately go through once the first train passes.,c:Cross quickly without checking other tracks.
note: At crossings with more than one track, one train passing can hide another coming from either direction. After the first train clears, stay stopped and look and listen carefully down all tracks. Proceed only when you can clearly see that every track is free of approaching trains.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Stop on the edge of the road and re-enter quickly.,b:Slow down gradually and gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Accelerate to regain control.,d:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually without hard braking. Once the car is under control and your speed is reduced, gently steer back onto the pavement. Sudden braking or sharp steering can cause a skid or loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, after you stop you should look which directions before proceeding?
options: a:Right first,b:Only check behind you for tailgating vehicles,c:Left first, then right, then left again before proceeding
note: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop, then look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you, then look right, and then look left again before proceeding. This sequence helps you detect vehicles that may be approaching quickly from the side that poses the most immediate risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, how should you indicate turns?
options: a:Use hand signals,b:Use your headlights,c:Use your horn
note: If your turn signals are not working, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show other drivers when you intend to turn or stop. Extend your left arm straight out for a left turn, bend your left arm up for a right turn, and bend it down for slowing or stopping.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, how should you yield on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.,b:Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass.,c:Drive as far toward the right side of the road as is safe and stop.
note: On a two-lane road, when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching, you must move as far to the right side of the road as is safe and come to a stop. Stopping on the right gives the emergency vehicle a clear path through the lane and helps prevent sudden, unpredictable movements by other drivers.

question: Which actions can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Talking on the phone,b:Changing the radio station,c:Eating
note: Distracted driving is caused by many activities that take your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving, such as eating, using a phone, or adjusting the radio. The best answer here is eating, but remember that all of these types of activities can be dangerous distractions and should be minimized while driving.

question: To help prevent collisions, you should:
options: a:Communicate with other road users by signaling and using warnings,b:Ignore other drivers on the road,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads
note: To help prevent collisions, you should clearly communicate your intentions to other road users. Use turn signals before turning or changing lanes, tap your brakes to warn of slowing, and use your horn or lights when needed. When others can predict what you will do, they can react safely and in time.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead, you should:
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake,b:Stare straight ahead at all times,c:Continuously scan the entire roadway and roadside
note: To prepare for hazards ahead, you should constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors regularly. This wide scanning helps you spot problems early—such as slowing traffic, pedestrians, or vehicles entering from side streets—so you have more time and space to react safely.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way,b:Call the other driver names out the window,c:Flash your lights to show them they're wrong
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm and create space. Slow down slightly, increase your following distance, or change lanes when safe to move away from them. Do not yell, gesture, or flash your lights, because that can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a crash.

question: What do working brake lights signal to drivers behind you?
options: a:Are changing lanes.,b:Are slowing down or stopping.,c:Are making a turn.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping so they can reduce speed and maintain a safe following distance. Keeping brake lights in good working order is essential to prevent rear-end collisions.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.,b:Follow the flagger's directions.,c:Assume the flagger is mistaken.
note: In construction zones, flaggers are authorized to direct traffic and their instructions have the same legal force as traffic signals or signs. You must follow their directions, even if they differ from normal traffic controls, to keep workers and drivers safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,b:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,c:Must slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed straight or turn, if not prohibited, but only when the intersection is clear and after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic when turning. It does not require you to slow or stop unless needed for safety.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk when using which device?
options: a:CD player,b:Radio,c:Cell phone
note: Cell phone use, including hands-free conversations and especially texting, is one of the most dangerous distractions because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from driving. Any in‑car device can distract you, but cell phones greatly increase crash risk.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding vehicle lights?
options: a:Use only parking lights,b:Use four-way flashers exclusively,c:Turn on your headlights (use low beams near other vehicles)
note: At dusk, in rain, or on overcast days, you should turn on your headlights so others can see you more easily. Use low beams when you are near other vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers, and never drive using only parking lights.

question: How does even a small amount of alcohol affect driving abilities?
options: a:Alcohol does not limit those abilities.,b:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can limit those abilities.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can limit your concentration
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your brain and body. It slows reaction time, reduces concentration, and harms judgment and coordination. Because you need all of these skills to drive safely, there is no completely safe amount of alcohol before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic while the traffic light is working, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to get the officer's attention.,b:Obey only the traffic light.,c:Follow the officer's directions.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions take priority over traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s directions, even if the traffic light shows a different signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Pass only on the right.,b:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic.
note: On a multilane highway, you must first make sure the lane you will use to pass is clear before moving over. Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and only change lanes when it is safe. Passing is usually done on the left unless signs or lane markings indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Drivers may choose to ignore the arrow if no other traffic is present,b:Drivers must stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow,c:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow
note: Arrows painted on the pavement show what movements are allowed or required from that lane, such as straight, left turn, or right turn. If you are in a lane with a turn-only arrow, you must make that movement, unless a traffic signal or sign specifically allows another action.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on which side must yield?
options: a:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way,c:The larger vehicle must yield
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right when both arrive at about the same time. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions by clearly assigning right‑of‑way.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:Railroad crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass. You may only cross them to make permitted turns (such as turning left into a driveway or side road) when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If another vehicle seems likely to hit you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Use your emergency lights.
note: If another vehicle may hit you, you should use your horn to warn the other driver. The horn is designed to quickly get another road user’s attention when there is a risk of a collision. Waving your arms is hard to see and not a reliable warning, and emergency flashers are for breakdowns or hazards, not immediate collision warning.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of injury in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways,b:Wear your seat belt,c:Limit your driving to weekdays
note: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective action you can take to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, reduce impact with the interior, and help you stay in control. Lane choice or when you drive cannot match the proven safety benefit of always buckling up.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes?
options: a:Force the bicyclist off the road.,b:Slow down and pass only when you can give at least 3 feet of clearance and it is safe to do so.,c:Honk and pass closely to quickly clear the rider.
note: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road, slow down and only pass when it is safe, giving the bicyclist at least 3 feet of clearance (or more at higher speeds, and more where state law requires). Never crowd, honk aggressively, or force a bicyclist off the road; treat them as you would a slow-moving vehicle and complete the pass only when you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'No stopping' sign generally allow you to do?
options: a:Stop only to avoid conflict with traffic or to obey a police officer or traffic signal,b:Stop briefly to unload packages,c:Stop to discharge passengers whenever you choose
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may not stop your vehicle at the curb or roadside for any reason other than to obey a traffic signal or officer, or to avoid a conflict with other traffic. You may not stop there to load or unload passengers or goods.

question: If borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Assume it functions like your usual car and drive away,b:Familiarize yourself with the vehicle’s controls and make sure it is safe to operate before driving,c:Hide any defects to avoid embarrassment
note: Before driving any unfamiliar vehicle, adjust the seat and mirrors, locate and test the lights, wipers, turn signals, and brakes, and make sure there are no safety‑critical defects. Do not drive a vehicle that has defects affecting safe operation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a steady yellow arrow, how should drivers respond?
options: a:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected movement is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely. If you are too close to the intersection to stop safely, proceed with caution and clear the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite-direction traffic, you should:
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left shortly,b:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately after passing,c:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle
note: When passing on a two‑lane road, use the left lane only long enough to pass. Return to your lane only when there is plenty of space ahead—typically when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate as quickly as possible,b:Reverse slowly,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians still in the intersection
note: A green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must first yield to pedestrians still in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: On slippery roads, which driving adjustment should you make?
options: a:Maintain the same gap as in normal conditions.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive as you would on dry roads.
note: On slippery roads, your stopping distance increases. To reduce the risk of a rear‑end collision, slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to stop.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump your brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should firmly pump the brakes to slow or stop quickly. Pumping helps prevent the wheels from locking, which allows you to maintain some steering control and reduces the chance of skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yield sign at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Yield only to traffic on your left.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Always come to a full stop regardless of conditions.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary to let traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection go first. You only proceed when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.,b:Let it go.,c:Flash your high beams at the driver.
note: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, create space, and continue driving defensively. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or any form of retaliation, as these can escalate into road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

question: Which of the following are effects of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:Loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment.,b:Increase in reaction speed.,c:Improved night vision.,d:Greater alertness.
note: Alcohol slows your brain and body, causing loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment and reaction time. Even small amounts can affect vision and decision-making, making it unsafe to drive.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White,b:Yellow and white,c:Yellow
note: Yellow pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and to mark the right edge of the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street, where should you begin the turn?
options: a:From the right lane.,b:From the center of the intersection.,c:From the left lane.
note: On a one-way street, all traffic moves in the same direction, so the leftmost lane is the correct lane from which to begin a left turn unless signs or lane markings direct you otherwise. Starting from the left lane keeps you aligned with proper turning paths and reduces conflicts with other vehicles.

question: Why is keeping a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.,b:Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
note: A space cushion is the open space you keep in front, behind, and to the sides of your vehicle. This extra space gives you time and room to see problems early and react smoothly to sudden stops, swerves, or mistakes by other drivers, greatly reducing your chances of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you permitted to pass another vehicle?
options: a:By using the highway shoulder when traffic is slow,b:On hills and curves if you think no oncoming car is near,c:Only where it is legal and safe — never on a hill or where your view is blocked
note: You may only pass where it is both legal and safe. Passing is generally prohibited on hills, curves, at intersections, railroad crossings, and anywhere you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic. Never use the shoulder to pass. Always obey pavement markings and signs that restrict passing.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or not permitted.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
note: A solid white line is used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. It means lane changes are discouraged and sometimes prohibited, such as before intersections or at freeway exits. A center line between opposite directions of travel is normally yellow, not white.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle,b:Only behind your vehicle,c:Only on the left and right sides
note: You should maintain a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle—front, rear, and both sides. This surrounding space gives you room to steer, brake, or accelerate away from danger and helps prevent collisions if another driver makes a mistake or traffic suddenly changes.

question: What are signs that require drivers to obey an instruction called?
options: a:Information signs,b:Warning signs,c:Regulatory signs
note: Regulatory signs are the signs that tell you laws and rules you must obey, such as speed limits, stop signs, and no‑turn signs. Ignoring these signs can result in tickets or other penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way road, you may not pass from either direction when the centerline is:
options: a:Single broken yellow,b:Double solid yellow,c:Combination solid and broken yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means that vehicles traveling in either direction are not allowed to pass. You may cross it only when turning left safely into or out of a driveway or side road, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: What should a driver do when taking a non-prescription drug before driving?
options: a:Drink alcohol instead to counteract effects,b:Assume no effect and drive normally,c:Read the drug label for warnings about driving
note: Many non‑prescription (over‑the‑counter) medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or otherwise less alert. Always read the label for driving or operating‑machinery warnings, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive.

question: If your car begins to skid, which direction should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:Toward the nearest curb regardless of skid direction.,b:Sharp opposite the skid.,c:To keep the front wheels straight.,d:In the direction you want the vehicle to go (into the skid).
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often called “steering into the skid.” As the vehicle starts to straighten out and you regain traction, carefully straighten the wheels to maintain control.

question: Which practice helps most to prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive through standing water as quickly as possible.,b:Keep cruise control on in wet weather.,c:Reduce speed when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. Slowing down in wet conditions and keeping your tires in good condition with proper tread and inflation are the best ways to reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What is the correct sequence before changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.,b:Check mirrors and immediately change lanes.,c:Signal and change lanes without checking, d:Check your blind spot only after you start changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal first to alert other drivers, then check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when it is clear and safe.

question: Where is it unlawful to park?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because you block pedestrians and cyclists and create a safety hazard. Legal parking is usually along the curb, within the required distance (often 12–18 inches, depending on state law), and only where signs and markings allow it.

question: What is the typical meaning of orange-colored traffic signs?
options: a:Regulatory instructions.,b:School zone warnings.,c:Work zone warnings.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead and tell drivers to slow down, be alert, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When entering a highway with other cars present.,b:When anything makes conditions less than perfect (such as wet roads, poor visibility, or heavy traffic).,c:Only if you see a police car.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed under ideal conditions, not a target speed you must always reach. You must slow down below the limit whenever conditions are less than perfect—such as rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, poor visibility, or damaged roads—so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: From a center left-turn lane, which maneuvers are permitted?
options: a:Use the lane to pass slow-moving traffic.,b:Use it to make U-turns only.,c:Drive through the lane as through-traffic.,d:Make left turns from the lane when indicated.
note: A center left‑turn lane is a shared lane used only for making left turns (and, where allowed by local law, certain U‑turns). You may not use it to pass other vehicles or to drive through as a regular travel lane; enter it briefly just before your turn and complete the turn safely.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Immediately accelerate and swerve back onto the road.,b:Gently ease off the accelerator,c:Stop immediately and get out of the vehicle.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the wheel. Gently ease off the accelerator so you slow down gradually, steer straight along the edge of the road, and only return to the pavement when traffic is clear and you can merge back smoothly. Sudden swerving or hard braking can cause you to lose control.

question: Which statement correctly describes alcohol’s effect on driving?
options: a:Alcohol increases coordination.,b:Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction times.,c:Alcohol will make you more alert.,d:Alcohol improves night vision.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and nervous system activity. It reduces coordination, slows reflexes and reaction time, and harms judgment and vision. Even small amounts can make you less able to react quickly to hazards, which is why any drinking before driving is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a required practice when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes.,c:Return to your lane as soon as you are next to the vehicle you passed.
note: When passing another vehicle on the left, you must check traffic carefully before moving out of your lane. Use your mirrors and then look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot, since another vehicle may be alongside you where mirrors cannot see. Signal before changing lanes, pass safely, and do not return to your lane until you can see the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: At a light rail intersection, what must you always do?
options: a:Ignore signals if no train is visible.,b:Drive around lowered gates if traffic is heavy.,c:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all traffic signals and signs.,d:Assume trains will yield to your vehicle.
note: At light rail or train intersections, you must always obey all warning signs, signals, and gates, and look carefully both ways down the tracks before crossing. Trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way, so never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train through the crossing.

question: What can happen if alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs, including many prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines, can greatly increase the effects of each. This can cause extreme drowsiness, poor coordination, slower reactions, and dangerously impaired judgment, making driving much more hazardous than using either substance alone.

question: A \No standing\" sign means you may:"
options: a:Never stop your vehicle there,b:Park there if the driver remains in the vehicle,c:Stop only temporarily to load or unload passengers
note: A 'No Standing' sign means you may stop only briefly to pick up or drop off passengers, but you may not wait there or park. You must leave as soon as passengers are safely in or out of the vehicle, and you may not load or unload cargo.

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, what is the safest action?
options: a:Lay down in the car and sleep,b:Stay in your car and wait for help,c:Get out and walk for help immediately
note: Remain in your vehicle to be more likely to be found; run the engine periodically for heat while ensuring the exhaust pipe is clear.

question: Driving without the required liability insurance is:
options: a:Not illegal but not recommended,b:Against the law,c:Without legal repercussions
note: Indiana law requires drivers to carry minimum liability insurance (commonly 25/50/25 limits); driving without it is illegal.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice before entering a roadway or crosswalk?
options: a:Enter at any time because drivers must stop for you,b:Always insist on your right-of-way over vehicles,c:Do not enter when vehicles are approaching; wait until it is safe to cross
note: Even when pedestrians have the right-of-way, do not step into traffic if vehicles are too close to stop safely; wait until it is safe.

question: How should you behave when approaching an accident scene?
options: a:Park and approach the accident to observe,b:Keep your attention on driving and keep moving unless you are involved or emergency help hasn't arrived,c:Stop to look at the scene
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; remain alert and continue safely past the area.

question: How would you characterize distracted driving?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers drivers, passengers, and others.,b:Very uncommon and not a major concern.,c:Harmless if only for a few seconds.,d:Required for multitasking drivers.
note: Distracted driving significantly increases crash risk; staying focused on driving and scanning the road is essential for safety.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait and only move it after police arrive.,b:Drive away immediately to avoid a traffic jam.,c:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,d:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: After a minor collision, move vehicles out of the flow of traffic if you can do so safely, while still identifying yourself and rendering assistance as required by law.

question: What must you confirm before passing another vehicle?
options: a:That you can brake and return to your lane if needed.,b:That you may cross over a solid lane marking.,c:That the passing lane is clear and passing is legal.,d:That the other driver is signaling to let you pass.
note: Before passing, you must be sure the passing lane is clear far enough ahead, that you have enough space and time to pass safely, and that passing is legal where you are. Always check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:At railroad crossings.,b:On hills and curves and in other areas where your view is limited.,c:At intersections with limited visibility.
note: Passing is prohibited in several high‑risk areas, including on hills and curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, at intersections, and at railroad crossings. Limited visibility and potential cross traffic make passing in these areas especially dangerous and often illegal.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:Always safe if you use high beams.,c:No different in risk.,d:More dangerous because visibility is reduced and hazards are harder to see.
note: Night driving reduces visibility and increases risks from glare and fatigued or impaired drivers; slow down and use appropriate lighting.

question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass before they reach your lane.,b:Flash your lights and continue slowly.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way.
note: Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and be prepared to come to a full stop when they are crossing in your path.

question: What should you do when driving on major highways to avoid fatigue or inattention?
options: a:Rely on cruise control to manage speed.,b:Maintain a steady gaze straight ahead to concentrate.,c:Stay alert by frequently scanning the road, using mirrors, and taking breaks when needed.
note: On major highways, you must stay alert and actively scan your surroundings to avoid fatigue and "highway hypnosis." Shift your focus between mirrors, instruments, and the road ahead, and take breaks as needed. Staring straight ahead without scanning reduces awareness, and cruise control does not prevent drowsiness.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Only honk at other drivers.,b:Only adjust the radio.,c:Take your eyes off the road,d:Only use cruise control.
note: Any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving increases your crash risk. Looking away from the road, even briefly, can prevent you from seeing hazards in time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front.,b:Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic moves.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through without stopping in it. Blocking the intersection can prevent cross traffic and emergency vehicles from moving and is illegal in many jurisdictions.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to crashes?
options: a:Following too closely,b:Excessive speed for conditions,c:Inattentive driving,d:All of the above
note: Following too closely, driving too fast for conditions, and inattentive or distracted driving are all common causes of crashes. Safe drivers leave enough following distance, adjust speed to weather and traffic, and keep their full attention on the road.

question: If a solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, what does that indicate?
options: a:Construction zone ends.,b:The road narrows ahead.,c:You must turn left soon.,d:There is an intersection ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the travel lane. When that line angles toward the center of the road, it means the usable lane is getting narrower and the shoulder is ending or shrinking, so you should be prepared for a narrower roadway.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:It is acceptable to follow motorcycles closely,b:A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than one with one rider,c:You must change lanes completely when you pass a motorcycle
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full traffic lane, just like any other vehicle. When you pass a motorcycle, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and pass as you would a car, leaving plenty of space and never sharing the lane side‑by‑side while passing.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights or sounding a siren, you must:
options: a:Yield and immediately pull to the right curb and stop,b:Continue driving in your lane,c:Slow down and keep moving
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren or flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as you safely can to the right edge or curb and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way do you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back slightly until the back of the front tire gently touches the curb. This way, if the brakes fail, the curb will stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid red arrow shown by a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the arrow's direction,b:The same as a circular red light — you must stop and may not turn in that direction,c:The arrow is not used in traffic signals
note: A solid red arrow means stop and remain stopped. You may not proceed or turn in the direction of the arrow while it is red, unless a sign specifically allows a turn on red after stopping and yielding, as permitted by that state’s law.

question: Which area is your vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:Directly behind your vehicle,b:You see it in your rearview mirror,c:An area you cannot see without moving your head
note: A blind spot is any area around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors and must turn or move your head to check. These areas are typically along the sides and slightly to the rear of your vehicle, where other vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles can be hidden from your mirror view.

question: If another driver is trying to pass your vehicle, how should you assist them?
options: a:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,c:Pull off the road.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain or slightly reduce your speed so they can pass safely. Do not signal them when to pass or pull off the road unnecessarily; simply create a safe, predictable situation so they can complete the pass and return to the lane safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a multi-lane street moving in your direction, where should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane road, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you are coming from. For example, if you are turning right from the right lane, you must enter the rightmost lane of the new road. This keeps traffic organized and reduces the chance of collisions with vehicles turning from other directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you pull over and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle with lights?
options: a:Always pull to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of the emergency vehicle's direction,b:Only if it is following you,c:Only if it is coming from the opposite direction
note: Pull to the right and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens whether they are approaching from front or behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver with left arm and hand extended upward is signaling they plan to:
options: a:Come to a stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Turn left.,d:Slow down.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn, and a left arm bent downward means slowing or stopping. A left arm and hand extended upward therefore indicates a right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver signaling with left arm and hand extended downward is indicating they intend to:
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Merge right.,d:Stop or slow down.
note: A left arm extended downward with the palm facing to the rear is the standard hand signal for slowing or stopping. Drivers behind should recognize this as a warning that the vehicle is reducing speed or coming to a stop.

question: When driving in general traffic, what is the safest practice regarding speed?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to get ahead.,b:Drive slower than everyone else.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits rather than much faster or slower.,d:Constantly fluctuate your speed to stay alert.
note: The safest practice is to travel at a speed that matches the general flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit. Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of collisions because it creates unexpected speed differences.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, it is usually best to:
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and then enter traffic.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely merged.,d:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and merge when a gap appears.
note: Freeway on-ramps are designed as acceleration lanes so you can increase speed to match freeway traffic. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge into a suitable gap, yielding to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,b:Turn the wheel sharply away from the skid.,c:Brake hard and keep the wheel straight.,d:Turn into oncoming traffic.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is generally the same direction the rear is skidding. This helps the tires realign with the direction of travel and regain traction.

question: How can the risk of hydroplaning be reduced while driving in wet conditions?
options: a:By driving through deeper water rather than shallower.,b:By driving more slowly.,c:By accelerating through standing water.,d:By maintaining properly inflated tires and avoiding sudden steering or braking in heavy rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, which can cause a complete loss of steering and braking control. The most effective way to reduce the risk is to slow down in wet conditions, especially in standing water, and ensure your tires are in good condition.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
