options: a:Move forward or fall back until the other driver can see you,b:Maintain your current speed and position,c:Stay in the blind spot to avoid merging confusion
note: Staying in another driver’s blind spot is dangerous because they may change lanes or turn without seeing you. Either gently speed up to move ahead or slow down to fall back so you are visible in their mirrors.

question: How can you avoid collisions caused by blind spots?
options: a:Honk before every lane change,b:Adjust your rearview mirror frequently while moving,c:Turn your head quickly to check the blind spot before changing lanes
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly beside and slightly behind your vehicle. Before changing lanes or turning, quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot so you do not move into a space already occupied by another vehicle.

question: Which headlights should you use in foggy weather?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Hazard lights only.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped). High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean when displayed for turn control?
options: a:It is never used as a traffic signal,b:Slow down and prepare for the arrow to change to red (same as a circular yellow),c:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated without yielding
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending. You should slow down and prepare to stop; you may complete the turn only if you are already in the intersection and can do so safely before the light turns red.

question: Which statement best describes how to respond to sudden changes in weather while driving?
options: a:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,b:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,c:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
note: When weather changes suddenly—such as rain, fog, snow, or strong wind—you must adjust your driving. Reduce speed, increase following distance, and stay extra alert to changing road and traffic conditions.

question: Which safety restraints are most effective in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt,b:Only an airbag,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag used together
note: Seat belts are your primary protection in a crash, and airbags are designed to work with them, not replace them. Wearing a lap and shoulder belt keeps you properly positioned so the airbag can cushion the impact without causing additional injury. Using both together greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death compared with using either one alone.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you lose control or need to warn another road user of imminent danger.,b:To express frustration when someone cuts you off.,c:To greet friends driving nearby.,d:Constantly while passing bicyclists.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision or warn others of immediate danger, such as if you lose control or another driver is about to hit you. Do not honk to show anger, greet friends, or for unnecessary noise, because that can startle other road users and create unsafe situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn others.,b:Swing to the right side of your lane to make the turn easier.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: Before turning left, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic, keep your wheels straight while waiting, and complete the turn only when the road and crosswalk are clear.

question: When changing lanes, what is the correct signaling practice?
options: a:Begin signaling while you are moving into the lane,b:Rely exclusively on mirrors without signaling,c:Signal in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas or 5 seconds on freeways) and not as you move into the lane
note: Signal well before you change lanes so other drivers have time to see what you plan to do. In many states this means signaling for at least 100 feet in city or residential areas, or for about 5 seconds on freeways. After signaling, check your mirrors and blind spot, then move into the lane only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to stop as if at a stop sign?
options: a:Yellow arrow.,b:Steady yellow light.,c:Flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop before the crosswalk or limit line, look for other vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Regulatory signs are usually which color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Green,b:White,c:Blue
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do (such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way). In the U.S., they are most commonly white with black or red symbols or lettering, and they must always be obeyed.

question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to give the vehicle space; if you cannot change lanes, slow down and pass cautiously.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Continue at the same speed in your lane.
note: Move over a lane if it is safe; otherwise slow down below the posted limit and pass carefully to provide room for responders.

question: What is the unique shape used for stop signs?
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Octagon.,c:Circle.
note: Stop signs are the only signs that use the octagon (eight-sided) shape. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,b:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,c:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child.
note: Always ensure all occupants are properly restrained; infants should ride in the rear and never in a rear-facing seat where a front airbag is active.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph take to stop?
options: a:Almost 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.,d:About 200 feet.
note: A fully loaded tractor‑trailer needs much more distance to stop than a passenger car. At about 55 mph, it can take close to 400 feet—more than the length of a football field—to come to a complete stop. This is why you should avoid cutting closely in front of large trucks.

question: When you notice other drivers acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact.,b:Distance yourself from the situation.,c:Don’t react with hand gestures.,d:All of the above.
note: When you encounter an angry or aggressive driver, your goal is to avoid escalating the situation and to keep yourself safe. Do not make eye contact, do not respond with gestures or yelling, and calmly create space between your vehicle and theirs. If possible, change lanes, slow down, or exit the roadway to distance yourself from the aggressive driver rather than engaging with them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit sign indicates:
options: a:Only a suggested speed.,b:The exact safe speed for all conditions.,c:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions for that roadway.
note: A posted speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions, not a suggested speed and not a guaranteed safe speed for every situation. You must often drive slower than the posted limit when conditions are poor, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or road construction, so that you can stop safely and maintain full control of your vehicle.

question: Which of these is NOT a factor in determining the distance it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Reaction distance.,b:Braking distance.,c:Steering ability.
note: Total stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It includes perception distance (seeing and recognizing the hazard), reaction distance (the distance traveled while you move your foot to the brake), and braking distance (the distance while the brakes are actually slowing the car). Steering ability does not directly change how far the car travels before stopping once you begin braking.

question: What does a dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and you may change lanes when safe.,b:Traffic is moving in opposite directions.,c:You may not pass.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so. Always check your mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder before moving into another lane.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor that affects blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,c:How much you drink.,d:How much time passes between drinks.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is mainly affected by how much alcohol you consume, your body weight, and how much time passes while your body processes the alcohol. The type of drink (beer, wine, or liquor) does not by itself determine BAC; what matters is the total amount of pure alcohol you take in and how quickly your body can eliminate it.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do when one train passes?
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
note: When there are multiple railroad tracks, a second train can come from either direction right after the first one passes. After the first train clears, stay stopped, look and listen carefully for another train on any track, and only proceed when you are sure all tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping,b:The driver on the left,c:The driver on the right
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Each driver should come to a complete stop, then the driver on the right proceeds first when it is safe.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what is the best action to take?
options: a:Stop driving.,b:Open your window.,c:Get some coffee.
note: Drowsy driving is extremely dangerous and cannot be reliably fixed by opening a window or drinking coffee. If you feel tired while driving, the safest action is to stop driving as soon as you can safely do so and rest before continuing.

question: Which is true about work zones?
options: a:They may be stationary or moving and require extra caution.,b:They are marked with black and white signs.,c:You do not need to slow down.
note: Work zones can be stationary (like a fixed construction area) or moving (like a line‑painting crew). They are usually marked with orange signs and cones. Drivers must slow down, follow posted work‑zone speed limits, and use extra caution for workers and equipment.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, remember they generally:
options: a:Require longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles,b:Require less distance to stop than smaller vehicles,c:Have a smaller turning radius than cars
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance to slow down and stop. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, give them extra space, and stay out of their blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, who must yield?
options: a:The merging driver may force their way into traffic.,b:No one needs to yield if traffic is light.,c:The driver entering the interstate should yield to vehicles already on it.,d:Drivers on the interstate must always yield to merging vehicles.
note: On entrance ramps, the driver who is entering the interstate must yield to vehicles already on the highway. Use the acceleration lane to match speed, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap; do not force your way into traffic or expect highway traffic to slow suddenly for you.

question: On average, your body eliminates alcohol at about what rate?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks an hour,b:One alcoholic drink an hour,c:Two alcoholic drinks an hour
note: A common guideline is that the body processes about one standard drink per hour, but this varies by person, size, sex, health, and food intake. Because you cannot reliably know your own rate, you should never use this as a way to decide if it is safe to drive after drinking.

question: What are the typical colors for warning signs that alert drivers to upcoming hazards?
options: a:White symbols on blue,b:Black symbols on a white background,c:Black symbols on a yellow background
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering, such as curve ahead or pedestrian crossing signs. Construction and maintenance warning signs are typically orange with black symbols, but they serve the same purpose of alerting you to hazards or changes in road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle,b:Honk your horn loudly,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes
note: Before passing, you must make sure it is safe: check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, signal, and then move into the passing lane. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming driver is headed into your lane, what should you do first?
options: a:Sound your horn, steer right, and brake to reduce impact.,b:Steer left and accelerate.,c:Brake and swerve left without warning.,d:Flash your lights and keep your speed.
note: If an oncoming vehicle is coming into your lane, your priority is to reduce the chance and severity of a head‑on collision. Try to get the other driver’s attention by sounding your horn, brake firmly to lower your speed, and steer to the right if you can safely leave the lane or use the shoulder. Steering left risks moving directly into the path of the oncoming vehicle or into other traffic.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should pedestrians walk on?
options: a:The side with the lightest traffic.,b:The side facing oncoming traffic.,c:The same side as traffic is moving.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see vehicles approaching them. This gives them a better chance to react if a driver does not see them or drifts toward the shoulder.

question: When roads may be slippery, you should:
options: a:Slow down and increase your following distance,b:Reduce your following distance,c:Always drive at the maximum posted speed
note: When roads may be slippery, you should slow down, increase your following distance, and avoid using cruise control so you can react quickly and smoothly. Driving at the maximum posted speed or using cruise control on slippery roads increases the risk of skidding and losing control.

question: You approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. Under which condition must you stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If the crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.,d:All of the above.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing if there is a stop sign, if the gate is down or coming down, or if the red lights are flashing. These controls mean a train may be approaching or is about to arrive, and you must not cross until it is clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a traffic signal showing a green arrow with a red light allow you to do?
options: a:You may only drive straight ahead.,b:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,c:You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, even if the other signal faces are red. You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow and only if the intersection is clear of pedestrians and other traffic.

question: When sleet or snow begins, what should you do while driving?
options: a:Turn off headlights to reduce glare.,b:Allow extra following distance and keep windshield and mirrors clear.,c:Drive at the posted speed to keep traffic flowing.
note: When sleet or snow begins, reduce your speed, increase your following distance, and keep your windshield, windows, and mirrors clear. Slippery conditions increase stopping distance, so you need more space and good visibility to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Drive out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching cars,c:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway
note: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must yield the right‑of‑way to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the main road. Wait until traffic is clear and it is safe to enter; do not force other road users to slow or change lanes for you.

question: Which actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Try to get to your destination as fast as possible.,b:Flash headlights repeatedly.,c:Allow extra travel time,d:Tailgate slower drivers to encourage them to move.
note: Allowing extra travel time helps you stay calm and avoid feeling rushed, which reduces the temptation to speed, tailgate, or make aggressive maneuvers. Courteous driving, obeying traffic laws, and avoiding confrontational behavior all help prevent road rage situations.

question: Where on the roadway do sections tend to freeze first and stay icy longest?
options: a:Areas shaded by trees or buildings,b:Flat sections of road,c:Curvy sections of road
note: Shaded areas of the road, such as those under trees, bridges, or next to buildings, freeze first and stay icy longer because they receive less sunlight. Use extra caution and reduce speed in these spots during cold or wet weather.

question: What effect does drinking coffee have on blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:It cancels the effects of alcohol.,b:It has no effect on BAC; only time reduces BAC.,c:It increases BAC temporarily.,d:It decreases BAC quickly.
note: Coffee does not change your blood alcohol concentration. It may make you feel more awake, but the alcohol in your system is removed only by your body over time. You can still be legally impaired even if you feel more alert after drinking coffee.

question: On which surfaces does your vehicle require a greater stopping distance?
options: a:On a wet or icy road.,b:On paved highways.,c:When driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases on wet, icy, or otherwise slippery surfaces because your tires have less traction. On dry, paved highways your brakes can grip the road better, so you stop in a shorter distance. Nighttime affects how far you can see, but the surface condition (wet/icy) is what directly increases the distance your vehicle needs to come to a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions.,b:The maximum posted speed only.,c:A speed that is safe for the conditions only.
note: You must always drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for current traffic, weather, and road conditions, even if that means driving slower than the posted speed limit. The posted speed is the maximum under ideal conditions, not a target speed you must reach.

question: If you must drive in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights to see farther.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: In fog, use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). Low beams and fog lights aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can actually make it harder to see.

question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Prescription medications, over-the-counter remedies, illegal drugs, and some cold/allergy medicines.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only marijuana.,d:Caffeine only.
note: Many drugs can impair driving, including prescription medications, over‑the‑counter remedies, illegal drugs, and some cold or allergy medicines. Always read labels and talk to your doctor or pharmacist; if a drug can cause drowsiness, slowed reaction, or confusion, you should not drive after taking it.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates what?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic in the lane next to the broken line, and not allowed for traffic in the lane next to the solid line. You may cross the broken line to pass when it is safe and legal, but you must not cross the solid yellow line to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign with no marked stop line or crosswalk, you may proceed after:
options: a:Slowing and verifying no cross traffic,b:Coming to a complete stop and verifying it is safe to proceed,c:Stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
note: At a stop sign without a stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. After stopping, look for other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards, and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line beside your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:You may pass when traffic is clear and it is safe to do so.,c:Never.,d:Only during daytime hours.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. If the broken yellow line is on your side of the centerline, you may cross it to pass another vehicle, but only when there is no oncoming traffic and you have enough space and visibility to pass safely.

question: Why should you avoid following other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly,b:You may miss the vehicle's turn signals,c:You may not see the road between the cars
note: Following too closely, or tailgating, is dangerous because you may not have enough time or distance to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you time to react to sudden changes and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Ignore the tracks if you don't see a train.,b:Drive around a lowered gate if traffic is light.,c:Look,d:Try to speed up to beat a train.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, always slow down, look, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop, and never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train. Trains are faster and closer than they may appear, and they cannot stop quickly.

question: How should you pass an animal you encounter on the roadway?
options: a:The driver should honk their horn.,b:Pass the animal as closely as possible.,c:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.
note: When you encounter an animal on or near the roadway, slow down and pass cautiously, giving it as much space as safely possible. Sudden movements or loud noises, like honking, can startle the animal and cause unpredictable behavior, increasing the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop even if clear,b:Slow down,c:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, you are not required to stop if the way is clear, but you must slow down, scan in all directions, and be prepared to yield. Treat it as a place of increased risk: cover the brake, check for pedestrians and cross‑traffic, and yield to vehicles already in the intersection or approaching from the right if you arrive at the same time.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels,c:Toward the right side of the road
note: When another driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the right side of the road and lane markings as a guide. This reduces glare while still letting you track your lane position and see hazards.

question: If you drink alcohol socially, which action best helps ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Take a cold shower before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Drink coffee before driving.
note: The only safe choice after drinking is not to drive. A sober driver, taxi, rideshare, or public transit keeps you and others safe. Cold showers, coffee, or other “sobering up” tricks do not lower your blood alcohol level or restore safe driving ability.

question: Which of the following substances can impair driving and lead to a DUII?
options: a:Only inhalants,b:Only beer and wine,c:Only illegal drugs,d:Alcohol and many other impairing substances, including illegal drugs, inhalants, and some medications
note: Driving under the influence laws apply to alcohol and many other substances, including illegal drugs, inhalants, and some prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines. Any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely can lead to a DUI. Among the listed options, alcohol is one clearly covered substance, but in reality the law is broader than just alcohol.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look only into the rearview mirror.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Look only into the side mirror.,d:Glance over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter.
note: Mirrors alone cannot show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move. This shoulder check lets you see into the blind spot and helps prevent collisions with vehicles you cannot see in your mirrors.

question: Driving while distracted by an activity usually has what effect on a driver?
options: a:Usually causes the driver to drive faster.,b:Is never dangerous.,c:Usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.
note: Distractions like texting, eating, or talking take your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. This usually slows your reaction time, so you notice hazards later and take longer to respond, which greatly increases your crash risk.

question: At night, which is hardest to see?
options: a:Other motorists,b:Pedestrians,c:Road signs
note: At night, pedestrians are the hardest to see because they are smaller, often wear dark clothing, and may not be in well‑lit areas. Headlights and streetlights make other vehicles and reflective road signs much easier to see than people on or near the roadway.

question: If the driver ahead is inattentive and talking to a passenger, what should you do?
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space because their safety margin is reduced.,b:Follow closely to monitor their behavior.,c:Signal them to drive faster.,d:Honk repeatedly to draw attention.
note: If a driver ahead seems distracted, increase your following distance. Extra space gives you more time to react if they brake suddenly, drift, or make mistakes. Avoid tailgating, honking, or trying to control their speed, as that can create more danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in line at a stop sign and cross traffic clears, what must you do?
options: a:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding,b:Proceed without stopping because you already stopped once,c:Roll slowly through the sign without stopping
note: You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or sign before entering the intersection. If you stopped back in a line of cars and then move up to the stop line, you must stop again before proceeding when it is safe.

question: When it begins to rain and visibility drops, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the rain faster.,b:Slow down and turn on your headlights to be seen by other drivers.,c:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless.
note: When rain begins, roads become slick and visibility drops. Slow down to maintain control and increase following distance, and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. If visibility becomes very poor, pull off the road safely and wait for conditions to improve.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which of the following is important?
options: a:Ensure the target lane is clear before moving into it.,b:Ignore your blind spot if mirrors look clear.,c:Change lanes without signaling to be quick.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move when you are sure the target lane is clear and you can change lanes smoothly and safely.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the center line.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Either side equally.
note: When an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, avoid looking directly at the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide so you are not blinded but can still keep your vehicle properly positioned.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which steady light will soon appear?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing red.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely; only proceed through the intersection if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass other cars when in a hurry,b:To turn left into or from a driveway or private road (or make permitted U-turns),c:To pass a slow-moving truck
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and generally mean no passing. You may cross them only to make a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or intersection, or to make a legal U-turn where allowed.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger,b:There is a stop sign controlling the crossing,c:Flashing red signals and crossing gates are operating
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger directs you to stop, when there is a stop sign at the crossing, or when flashing red lights and/or lowered gates indicate a train is approaching. Always obey all warning devices and only proceed when you are sure the tracks are clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, how should you usually merge?
options: a:Stop first then creep into traffic.,b:Use your horn continuously while merging.,c:Enter well below traffic speed and force others to slow.,d:Signal, use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed, and merge into a safe gap while yielding to highway traffic.
note: When entering a highway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge into a safe gap. You must yield to vehicles already on the highway and should not stop in the acceleration lane unless absolutely necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and hold your lane without allowing extra space.,b:Maintain your lane and, if needed, slow down slightly to create space in front so the other vehicle can pass and return safely.,c:Speed up to get away.
note: If a driver behind you wants to pass, you should help them do it safely. Maintain your lane and, if needed, slow down slightly to create more space in front of you so they can return to the lane safely after passing. Do not speed up to block or race the passing vehicle.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign usually indicates:
options: a:Road hazard or warning sign,b:An interstate route sign,c:School crossing sign
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to hazards or special conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or merging traffic. School crossing signs are typically pentagon-shaped, not diamond-shaped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow centerline, what does that tell you?
options: a:You are entering a two-way road where passing is permitted when safe,b:You are on a one-way road,c:The road is under repair
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions on a two-way road. You may cross a broken yellow line to pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so, but you must still check for oncoming traffic and other hazards.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Cross at your own risk if no signals are active.,b:Honk and proceed.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,d:Slow and then cross quickly.
note: If a train is close enough to be dangerous, you must not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed and you can see clearly in both directions before crossing. Trains cannot stop quickly, and trying to beat a train is extremely dangerous and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a flashing red traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign — come to a full stop and proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping,c:Continue through if there is no crossing traffic
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: How should a lap belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Hidden under the seat,b:Loose across your stomach,c:Snugly and low across your hip bones, not your stomach
note: The lap belt should fit low and snug across your hip bones, touching the upper thighs, not across the soft part of your stomach. This positioning helps the belt hold your body against the stronger pelvic bones in a crash and reduces the risk of internal injuries.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line separating lanes is which of the following?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.,d:Solid white line (generally no passing or lane change discouraged).
note: You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe because it separates lanes moving in the same direction. Solid or double solid yellow lines generally mean no passing because they separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid white line usually discourages lane changes, especially near intersections or on-ramps.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:The parked car will remain stationary,b:The driver may open their door into your path,c:The driver will signal before opening the door.
note: When passing a recently parked vehicle, you should expect that a door could open suddenly or a person could step out. Slow down, leave extra space, and be prepared to stop or move away from the vehicle if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it required to signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb?
options: a:Yes — signaling is required by law and is a good driving habit.,b:Only if other traffic is present.,c:Not necessary if you think it is obvious.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb, even if you think no one is around. Signaling at least the last 100 feet before your turn (and more at higher speeds) lets other road users anticipate your actions and helps prevent collisions.

question: What is a \No zone\" for large vehicles?"
options: a:A designated no-passing area,b:A one-way traffic area,c:The large blind spots alongside and behind a truck or bus
note: A "No-Zone" is the large blind spot area around a truck or bus where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. These zones are along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of large vehicles. You should avoid lingering in these areas because the truck or bus driver may not know you are there and could change lanes or stop suddenly without seeing you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what sequence of checks should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles without checking mirrors.,b:Check both side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,c:Check your side view mirror only.
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. This combination of mirror checks and a shoulder glance helps ensure there is no vehicle hidden where your mirrors cannot see.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: When an oncoming vehicle is approaching at night, you must use low beam headlights so you do not blind the other driver. High beams are only for use when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not following another vehicle too closely.

question: On slippery roads, how should you adjust your driving?
options: a:Slow down and drive more slowly than the posted speed if conditions require.,b:Drive faster to get through slippery areas quickly.,c:Maintain the posted speed exactly at all times.,d:Turn off traction control immediately.
note: On slippery roads, such as in rain, snow, or ice, you should slow down below the posted speed if needed and increase your following distance. Reduced speed gives you more time to react and helps prevent skids because your tires have less grip on the road.

question: When may you legally cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:During daylight hours only.,b:Any time there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Only to turn into or out of a driveway
note: A solid yellow centerline generally means no passing, but you may cross it to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or business when it is safe. You may not cross it just to pass another vehicle, even if there is no oncoming traffic.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Maintain good tread depth, proper tire inflation, and reduce speed in rain,b:Only ensure tires are properly inflated,c:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. You reduce this risk by keeping good tire tread, maintaining proper tire pressure, and slowing down in the rain so your tires can push water away and maintain contact with the pavement.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,c:Slow down until it passes you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It improves reaction time.,b:It causes you to always drive more carefully.,c:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and focus on driving tasks.
note: Stress can distract you from the road, narrow your attention, and slow your reactions. It can make you more likely to miss signs, signals, and hazards. If you are very upset or stressed, it is safer to delay driving until you can concentrate fully on driving tasks.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service station.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Brake hard immediately to stop as quickly as possible.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly to keep the vehicle straight, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the car slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking until you have the vehicle under control, then carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you allow?
options: a:Give the motorcycle the full lane; a motorcycle is entitled to the entire lane.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,c:Allow the motorcycle only half a lane.,d:Require the motorcyclist to ride in the center of the lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane just like any other vehicle. Give them the entire lane and do not try to share the lane beside them, because they need room to maneuver and maintain balance and a safety cushion.

question: After a school bus finishes unloading and its stop arm is withdrawn, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed immediately once the bus moves,b:Wait until the children wave at you,c:Watch for children walking near the roadway before proceeding
note: After a bus stops unloading, be alert for children who may be near or crossing the road before you proceed.

question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Stop and check all directions.,c:Treat it like a yield sign.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed if it is safe, but you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection. Do not enter the intersection if it is blocked, and be prepared for the light to change to yellow.

question: What is the primary cause recorded in over 93% of fatal collisions?
options: a:Malfunctioning traffic signals.,b:Unsafe road conditions exclusively.,c:Weather alone.,d:Driver action or error.
note: Studies show that the vast majority of fatal crashes are linked to driver behavior, such as speeding, distraction, impairment, or failing to yield. Road and weather conditions matter, but driver decisions and errors are the primary recorded cause in most fatal collisions.

question: How should you safely cross a railroad track?
options: a:Only cross when the red light is flashing.,b:Rely solely on your vehicle's radio to detect trains.,c:Listen and look both ways,d:Cross rapidly when you hear a distant train.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Obey all warning signs, lights, and gates. Never cross until you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to fully clear the tracks on the other side.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers who:
options: a:Consistently check their mirrors and blind spots,b:Yield the right-of-way frequently,c:Drive too fast for conditions
note: Driving too fast for conditions—such as rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road surfaces—is a frequent cause of crashes. Even if you are below the posted speed limit, you must slow down when conditions reduce visibility or traction so you can stop safely if hazards appear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an intersection controlled by signs at the same time, which driver must yield?
options: a:Either driver at random.,b:The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.,c:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
note: At an intersection controlled by stop or yield signs, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps avoid confusion and collisions by clearly assigning right‑of‑way.

question: Which statement about driving on a wet roadway is true?
options: a:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:As you drive faster on a wet road, your tires lose contact with the road and the risk of hydroplaning increases.
note: On wet roads, as your speed increases, your tires ride higher on the water and lose contact with the pavement, greatly increasing the risk of hydroplaning. Always slow down on wet surfaces, especially in heavy rain or standing water.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn loudly and back out slowly.,b:Rely only on mirrors and cameras.,c:Get out and walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: Before backing where children may be present, walk behind your vehicle to check for kids, toys, or other obstacles that may be too low to see in mirrors or cameras. After checking, back out slowly and be prepared to stop immediately.

question: Which actions help reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Avoid speeding on wet roads.,b:Ignore tire tread condition.,c:Drive faster through puddles.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, slow down on wet roads, avoid sudden steering or braking, and keep your tires properly inflated with good tread. Lower speeds and good tires help your tires maintain contact with the road surface.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red light, you should:
options: a:Honk to warn the pedestrians.,b:Speed up past the pedestrians.,c:Stop and allow pedestrians to cross safely.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing against the signal. Stop and allow them to cross safely, then proceed when the crosswalk is clear.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass, and the bicyclist may swerve into traffic,b:Bicycles always have the right-of-way,c:You are moving slower than a bicycle
note: Bicyclists are vulnerable and may need to swerve suddenly to avoid potholes, debris, or opening car doors. When you pull out to pass, oncoming drivers may not see you in time, especially if you move out quickly. Always pass with plenty of space and only when it is safe and clear.

question: Which actions help you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Not drive if you are tired.,b:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:All of the above.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you should use several safety habits together: avoid driving when you are tired, make sure your headlights are clean and working properly, and increase your following distance so you have more time to react. All of these actions help you drive more safely at night.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert to motorcycles on the road?
options: a:Motorcycles must always ride on the shoulder.,b:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.,c:Motorcycles never use headlights.,d:Motorcyclists are always less skilled than car drivers.
note: Motorcycles are much smaller than cars and can be hidden easily in blind spots or by other vehicles. They can also appear farther away and moving slower than they really are, making it harder to judge their speed and distance. Always check mirrors and blind spots carefully and give motorcycles extra space.

question: On slick roads you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly to avoid slipping,b:Change lanes quickly,c:Take turns more slowly than usual
note: On slick or slippery roads, your tires have less grip, so sudden movements can cause skids. Slow down before turns and curves and steer and brake gently. Taking turns more slowly helps you maintain traction and control of the vehicle.

question: Which driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in your driveway with the engine running,b:Slowing down gradually and anticipating stops,c:Accelerating quickly from stops
note: To conserve fuel, look ahead and anticipate stops so you can slow down gradually instead of braking hard at the last moment. Smooth, steady acceleration and braking use less gasoline than rapid starts, sudden stops, or unnecessary idling.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection with blocked views, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane clears,b:Proceed when an oncoming driver waves you across,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before starting the turn
note: When turning left at a multilane intersection where your view is blocked, you must not start the turn until you can clearly see every lane you must cross. This ensures you won’t be surprised by a hidden vehicle in another lane and can complete the turn without stopping in the path of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection,b:Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked,c:Stop completely
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the proper response?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and drive to a safe place to stop.,b:Turn off your headlights and stop immediately in the travel lane.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and continue at the same speed.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer but it will take much more effort. Keep a firm grip on the wheel, reduce your speed, signal, and carefully move to the side of the road or a safe place to stop so the problem can be checked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a steady red traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop; you may turn right unless a sign prohibits it.,b:Drive through the intersection if no other vehicles are present.,c:Proceed unless a police officer is nearby.,d:Slow down and roll through if the way seems clear.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line. After stopping and yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians, you may turn right unless a sign specifically says that right turns on red are not allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass on a two-way, two-lane street?
options: a:When you are able to partially drive on the shoulder,b:When your vehicle can reach the necessary passing speed only,c:Only if you can clearly see the road ahead and return to your lane before oncoming traffic appears
note: On a two-way, two-lane road, you may pass only when passing is legal and you can clearly see far enough ahead to complete the pass safely. You must be able to move into the oncoming lane, pass, and return to your lane before meeting any oncoming traffic.

question: A crossbuck sign at a roadway indicates:
options: a:No passing zone,b:School zone,c:Railroad crossing
note: A crossbuck is the white X-shaped sign found at railroad crossings. It tells drivers they are at a railroad crossing and must yield to any approaching train, slowing or stopping as needed before the tracks.

question: What is an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who checks mirrors regularly.,b:Someone who maintains eye contact with a passenger.,c:Someone who stares off the road,d:Someone who only watches the car ahead.
note: An inattentive driver is not scanning the whole traffic scene. Focusing only on the car ahead and failing to check mirrors, side areas, and the road further ahead is a form of inattention that greatly increases the risk of missing hazards.

question: What does a green arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same as a circular green but only on one-way streets.,b:Traffic in the lane indicated may proceed but must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.,c:You may go straight only.
note: A green arrow means traffic in the lane controlled by that arrow may proceed, but only in the direction the arrow points. It is a protected movement, but you must still yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.

question: What happens to your field of vision as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:It becomes more sensitive to peripheral movement.,b:It decreases,c:It increases dramatically.,d:It remains unchanged.
note: As your speed increases, your useful field of vision narrows. You see less to the sides and must work harder to scan for hazards, which is why high speeds require extra attention and longer following distances.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Signal, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your rearview and side mirrors, and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This ensures the lane is clear where mirrors alone cannot show.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over the shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the outside mirror on that side.
note: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to be sure no vehicle is hidden in your blind spot.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Only set the parking brake.,b:Leave the engine running briefly.,c:Leave the radio on to deter theft.,d:Turn off the engine and secure the vehicle so it cannot move or be easily used by others.
note: When unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition and remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a road means:
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not permitted.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Drivers may change lanes across a broken white line when it is safe to do so and after signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Recommended speeds for inexperienced drivers only.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed for ideal conditions; you must slow below the limit when conditions require.,c:Potential driving speeds for the area only.,d:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions. You must always drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions, which may be well below the posted limit in bad weather, heavy traffic, or poor visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check your mirrors and turn on your directional signal before changing lanes.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and then look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look only in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter to check your blind spot. This over-the-shoulder check helps you see vehicles that mirrors may miss.

question: When should you signal?
options: a:Only at intersections,b:Changing lanes,c:Only when making major turns
note: Use your turn signal any time you change lanes, turn, merge, or enter/leave traffic so other road users know what you plan to do. Signaling early and consistently helps prevent crashes and is required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers when entering traffic?
options: a:Only when they are on a road to your left,b:Only when your signal is green,c:When entering from a garage
note: When entering a road from private property such as a garage, driveway, or alley, you must stop if needed and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. Traffic on the main road has the right‑of‑way until it is clearly safe for you to enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a sudden stop in the middle of the intersection.,b:Be prepared to stop safely; do not speed up to beat the red light.,c:Accelerate to beat the red.,d:Continue without changing speed in all cases.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you can stop safely before the intersection, you should slow down and stop rather than speeding up. Only continue through if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

question: If your vehicle with ABS begins to skid on a slippery surface, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the gas pedal,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger,c:Pump the brakes repeatedly
note: With antilock brakes (ABS), press the brake pedal firmly and hold it while you steer in the direction you want to go. ABS automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup, so you should not pump the pedal yourself.

question: For persons age 21 or older, what BAC is illegal to drive at or above?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In all U.S. states, it is illegal for drivers age 21 or older to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. Even lower levels can affect driving, but 0.08% is the standard legal limit for impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin slowing down as you exit a highway?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane,b:On the main road just before the exit lane,c:Only when you see a toll booth
note: On highways, maintain the normal speed of traffic while you are still in the main travel lanes. Move safely into the exit (deceleration) lane first, and then begin slowing down within that lane so you do not disrupt through traffic behind you.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but not using emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in the center of the road.,b:Continue driving normally; you do not need to clear a path.,c:Pull over immediately and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: You are required to yield and clear a path only when an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is simply driving behind you with no emergency signals, continue driving normally, obeying all traffic laws and not making sudden or unpredictable moves.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, what is recommended?
options: a:Keep driving and listen to loud music.,b:Stop and rest every two hours or when drowsy.,c:Do arm exercises without stopping.,d:Drive with one eye closed occasionally.
note: On long trips, stop regularly—about every two hours—or sooner if you feel drowsy. Get out, walk around, or rest. Driving while tired greatly reduces your reaction time and judgment and can be as dangerous as driving under the influence.

question: What device is sometimes used on highways to indicate which lanes to use for turning?
options: a:Stop signs in the middle of the road.,b:Flashing red lights only.,c:Lane-use arrows painted on pavement or on overhead signs.,d:White lines on the side of the road.
note: Lane-use arrows, either painted on the pavement or shown on overhead signs, tell you which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. Always choose your lane early and follow the arrows to avoid sudden lane changes near intersections.

question: Extra caution is required when approaching a pedestrian carrying a white cane because:
options: a:They are likely blind or visually impaired,b:They are a police officer,c:They are deaf
note: A white cane is used by people who are blind or visually impaired. When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must use extra caution, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop so they can cross safely.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, you should:
options: a:Stop at a safe distance and look for a train,b:Slow down and look for a train,c:Look for a train then speed up to clear the crossing
note: Flashing railroad signals mean a train is approaching. You must stop before the tracks, typically no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail, and wait until the lights stop flashing and any gates are fully raised before proceeding. Never try to beat the train by speeding up.

question: When driving in bad weather, how should you adjust following distance?
options: a:Keep the same following distance as in good weather,b:Increase your following distance,c:Decrease your following distance
note: In rain, snow, fog, or other poor conditions, it takes longer to see hazards and to stop. Increasing your following distance gives you more time and space to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly, reducing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Defensive driving is best defined as:
options: a:Getting ahead of poor drivers in traffic,b:Following the vehicle ahead closely to anticipate stops,c:Identifying dangerous situations and taking steps to avoid accidents
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning for potential hazards, predicting what other road users might do, and adjusting your speed, position, and actions early to avoid collisions. It focuses on prevention, not aggression or following too closely.

question: If you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazards and keep driving.,b:Speed up to avoid it.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials.

question: If a transit bus signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Yield and allow the bus to merge safely,b:Honk to let the driver know you're there,c:Speed up to pass before the bus merges
note: Transit buses often make frequent stops and need space to re-enter traffic. When a bus signals to merge back in, you should yield by adjusting your speed or changing lanes if safe, allowing the bus to re-enter smoothly and safely.

question: What is the best practice to ensure safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, walk behind and around your vehicle to look for children, pets, and objects that may be in your blind spots. Mirrors alone cannot show everything behind you, so checking the area on foot first is the safest practice.

question: Solid white stop lines painted across traffic lanes indicate:
options: a:In curves and on hills,b:Where drivers must stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks,c:Next to churches and schools
note: A solid white stop line across the lane shows where you must stop at an intersection or before a crosswalk when required by a sign, signal, or traffic officer. Your front bumper should not cross this line when you are stopped.

question: What is the most common cause of hydroplaning?
options: a:Frequent sudden stops.,b:Driving too fast for wet road conditions.,c:Making sudden turns.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. Driving too fast for wet conditions makes it easier for water to build up under the tires, causing loss of steering and braking control.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent it from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver shows the left arm and hand extended upward, what does that hand signal indicate?
options: a:Turn right.,b:Continue straight ahead.,c:Turn left.
note: Standard hand signals are: left arm straight out for a left turn, left arm bent upward at the elbow for a right turn, and left arm bent downward for slowing or stopping. An arm and hand extended upward indicates a right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the minimum liability auto insurance limits required in Indiana?
note: Indiana law requires drivers to carry liability insurance with minimum limits of 25/50/25: $25,000 for bodily injury per person, $50,000 per accident, and $25,000 for property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Indiana's point system, how long do active points remain on your driving record from the conviction date?
options: a:1 year,b:2 years,c:3 years,d:5 years
note: Points assessed for traffic violations remain active on your Indiana driving record for two years (24 months) from the conviction date.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How many demerit points can you have credited (removed) from your Indiana driving record by completing a BMV-approved Driver Safety Program (DSP)?
options: a:2 points,b:4 points,c:6 points,d:8 points
note: Successful completion of a BMV-approved Driver Safety Program (DSP) grants a 4-point credit on your Indiana driving record. You can receive this credit once every three years.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Indiana's Move Over law, if you cannot change lanes safely when passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and drive on the shoulder,b:Reduce your speed to at least 10 mph below the posted limit and proceed with caution,c:Stop completely on the highway,d:Honk your horn to warn the workers
note: If you are unable to change lanes safely when passing a stopped emergency, utility, or maintenance vehicle, you must reduce your speed to 10 mph below the posted speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Indiana, you are legally required to immediately report a traffic accident to the police if it results in injury, death, or property damage of at least:
note: Under Indiana law, any crash resulting in injury, death, or apparent property damage of $1,000 or more must be reported immediately to the police.
